title: Real-Time GUI and UDP Communication Framework for Dual Capacitive Smart Insole Gait Acquisition
venue: 2026 2nd International Conference on Smart Mechatronics (ICSMech)
abstract: This paper presents the real-time acquisition and communication framework of a dual capacitive smart-insole system for gait measurement. Two ESP32-based wireless nodes and a Python GUI communicate over Wi-Fi UDP for tare calibration, synchronization, visualization, and CSV logging. Each insole provides eight multiplexed capacitive channels and two IMUs. The study asks whether this low-cost architecture can provide sufficiently stable timing despite very fast multiplexed capacitive readout, host-side polling jitter, and non-zero network latency. Evaluation on 90 left-foot and 90 right-foot CSV files from five subjects shows a timing distribution composed of a stable nominal regime plus sparse long-interval disturbances. After steady-state filtering, the operating regime becomes tightly concentrated near the intended host polling behavior, indicating that the framework is sufficiently stable for research-grade smart-insole acquisition.

title: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition for LED Control using CNN and Arduino
venue: 2025 Second International Conference on Intelligent Technologies for Sustainable Electric and Communications Systems (iTech SECOM)
abstract: This paper introduces a Hand Gesture Recognition System using OpenCV and deep learning to improve the interactivity between human and computer. The system uses a video feed to recognize and interpret hand gestures, so it has an interactive means of controlling applications and devices. It uses MediaPipe to extract accurate hand landmarks and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for efficient gesture classification. The use of OpenCV makes frame processing and sorting gestures quick, allied with a Python-based backend to assure fluency in execution. The system is capable of detecting and differentiating multiple static gestures with an accuracy which makes possible applications suitable as virtual controllers, assistive technology or touchless interfaces. It is also very convenient due to its real-time nature and easy for the user to use hence an effective tool in today's current interactive systems.

title: Real-Time Hand Gesture Replication System using 3D Modelling Software
venue: 2020 IEEE Students Conference on Engineering & Systems (SCES)
abstract: This article proposes a method to replicate the realtime hand gesture movements on a 3-D simulation software called Blender 3D. It is a gaming engine simulation software that is also used for simulation of 3D models. A special glove is designed for this purpose, and each finger on the glove is fitted with a flex sensor. Flex sensors (or bend sensors) are two-terminal sensors and work just like a variable resistor in which resistance changes upon bending. The voltage drop across the flex sensor is passed through a microcontroller (Arduino used here) into the Blender-3D. A 3D model of a human hand is also needed to be designed in the Blender- 3D. This model will be used to observe our hand movements on the software. Python code and Arduino code is to be written to guide the hand movement based on the flex sensor values. The project can be used in numerous ways, like helping especially abled people replace their hands with bionic hands which can be suited for their personal hand structure or designing games that can be played with gesture movements of the finger.

title: Real-Time Hand Tracking and Trajectory Gesture Recognition
venue: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: With the advent of modern technologies, traditional input devices such as the mouse, keyboard, and remote control are becoming obsolete due to their lack of flexibility. In today's society, humans primarily communicate with computers using body language or voice commands, which are now widely integrated into most electronic devices. Hand gestures, in particular, are highly effective in human-computer interaction due to their natural expressiveness. However, vision-based hand gesture recognition systems face challenges such as complex backgrounds, illumination variations, and other environmental factors. Additionally, reliably detecting and tracking hands to extract trajectory information from video scenes remains a difficult task due to the diverse appearances of human hands, including variations in hand shapes, skin colors, illuminations, orientations, and scales in color images. Distinguishing between meaningful and meaningless motion trajectories further complicates dynamic hand gesture recognition. To address these challenges, a real-time hand tracking and gesture recognition system is proposed. This project implements real-time hand tracking and landmark estimation using Python, OpenCV, and MediaPipe. Hand trajectory gesture recognition is then achieved using a customized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with three convolutional layers, one flatten layer, and two fully connected layers. The network is built and trained using Matlab and trained model is exported to python using scipy.io module for model deployment. The model was trained on the MNIST dataset, which consists of 10 numeric gestures (0–9) with an overall testing accuracy of 97. 21%. When implemented on trajectory-based gestures, the system yielded an accuracy of 87.1%.

title: Real-time health monitoring system design based on optical camera communication
venue: 2021 International Conference on Information Networking (ICOIN)
abstract: A dramatic increase in internet-of-things-based remote health monitoring systems can be observed in recent times. The majority of them use a technology based on radio frequency (RF), whose adverse effects on human health are continuously addressed in the literature. We have designed a system using a pulse oximeter sensor to monitor the health conditions of the patient and transmit data through the LED and received using a camera. The camera captures the image and extracts the data from the receiver in the Python environment. The data is modulated using a color shift keying technique, and based on the different colors the data is retrieved from the receiver.

title: Real-time Heart Disease Prediction System using Multilayer Perceptron
venue: 2021 2nd International Conference for Emerging Technology (INCET)
abstract: Stroke, Heart Failure, Arrhythmia, and myocardial infarction are the most common cardiovascular diseases which record high mortality rates around the world. Heart defects are not detected in the early stages due to the impractical costs of the tests available. Thus, a fast, real-time, and reliable system that predicts the chances of a patient having heart disease in an optimized manner is required.In this research, a Neural Networks model using a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) is proposed for the prediction system. Experimental analysis resulted in an accuracy of 85.71% for UCI Heart Disease dataset and 87.30% for Cardiovascular Disease dataset. When compared to previous research the increase in accuracy was approximately 12-13%. A simple web application tool is also developed using python programming to test the prediction system. This research works towards making a comprehensible tool for medical professionals as well as common people.

title: Real-Time Human Detection and Tracking System: A Novel Comparative Study of Centroid Tracking, Single Shot Detection and YOLO Algorithms
venue: 2023 1st International Conference on Advanced Engineering and Technologies (ICONNIC)
abstract: This study presents the development of a device capable of implementing social distancing monitoring using Centroid Tracking Algorithm, Single Shot Detector (SSD), and YOLO which run on powerful computers or servers with dedicated GPU s due to their complex computations and resource-intensive deep learning models. This is to support the government's continuous policy on social distancing in public places in Metro Manila and regions that still have the highest COVID-19 cases. Using as few people as possible due to restrictions on physical spaces, this study also developed a novel test that would compare the two said algorithms for optimal an Intel NUC hardware-based object detection and object tracking system with a focus on counting people. Using real-time footage from a CCTV camera with OpenCV and Python, the data from the simulations was then sent and analyzed to the web server cloud platform, ThingSpeak. Overall, it was determined that YOLO algorithm has less errors than the Centroid Tracking + SSD Algorithm and was thus more compatible with the developed system.

title: Real-time Hybrid Dashboard and App for Mpox Outbreak Surveillance
venue: 2023 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC)
abstract: With the continuous rise in the global threat of infectious diseases, surveillance systems have become powerful tools for monitoring the development and transmission patterns of fast-changing disease outbreaks, by public health officers. These surveillance systems typically track relevant epidemiological data such as number of cases, fatality rates, hot spots, and in most cases, evaluate the impact of public health intervention strategies in these locations. Data from these surveillance apps can also be used for efficient emergency response preparatory logistics, as well as early containment. In this paper, we presents a modular, open-source, GIS-enabled, web-based dashboard and mobile app that are capable of visualizing and identifying epidemiological patterns for any infectious disease of interest, in real time. These visualizations can be in the form of GIS maps, charts, and other metrics to track certain indicators. Python and Streamlit library are used to manage the frontend of the application. Data from the 2022 Mpox outbreak in the United States were used to evaluate the application. Nongovernmental organizations or other community-based groups can leverage on, and adapt this dashboard to monitor the spread of any quick-onset disease outbreak in their regions.

title: Real-Time Image and Video Processing Applications Using Raspberry Pi
venue: 2022 IEEE 1st Industrial Electronics Society Annual On-Line Conference (ONCON)
abstract: Image and video processing applications have significant importance in many areas which are the industrial and medical applications, especially the vehicular technology. To provide safe driving, Driving Assistance Systems (DAS) including detection and tracking of a road situation, objects and behavior of the driver should be considered by using the image processing algorithms. Since these applications need the processors having high speed and power, a Raspberry Pi platform meeting these specifications is used in this study. A Canny edge detector which is one of the important edge detection methods, face and eye detection, the road line tracking, motion detection, and object detection applications are handled. Conversely the studies in the literature which are separately examined these techniques, all of them are realized as a real-time based on the Rapberry Pi according to a video image taken by a camera. For this reason, OpenCv and TensorFlow libraries having widely computer vision algorithms and Python software language are used. It is observed that the results of all image and video processing applications are successful and satisfying. As a result, a safe and comfortable driving can be provided thanks to the proposed methods.

title: Real-time Implementation of RMNv2 Classifier in NXP Bluebox 2.0 and NXP i.MX RT1060
venue: 2020 IEEE Midwest Industry Conference (MIC)
abstract: With regards to Advanced Driver Assistance Systems in vehicles, vision and image-based ADAS is profoundly well known since it utilizes Computer vision algorithms, for example, object detection, street sign identification, vehicle control, impact cautioning, and so on., to aid sheltered and smart driving. Deploying these algorithms directly in resource-constrained devices like mobile and embedded devices etc. is not possible. Reduced Mobilenet V2 (RMNv2) is one of those models which is specifically designed for deploying easily in embedded and mobile devices. In this paper, we implemented a real-time RMNv2 image classifier in NXP Bluebox 2.0 and NXP i.MX RT1060. Because of its low model size of 4.3MB, it is very successful to implement this model in those devices. The model is trained and tested with the CIFAR10 dataset.

title: Real-Time Implementation of Spatial Audio on FPGA Using Interaural Time Difference and Amplitude-Driven Perceptual Depth
venue: 2024 First International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Signal Processing (ICECSP)
abstract: This paper describes the real-time implementation of spatial audio effect using Basys-3 field programmable gate array (FPGA). The spatial audio effect in this paper is obtained by varying the azimuthal sound direction using interaural time difference (ITD) and amplitude-driven perceptual depth effect. In addition to the Basys-3 FPGA board, a peripheral module accessory (PMOD) I2S2 is used to take analog audio data from a mobile phone through an auxiliary-to-auxiliary cable and digitize it. This digitized data is then processed using a Verilog module and converted back to analog audio data using (PMOD) I2S2 to play the output audio through a pair of headphones. The introduction of varying azimuthal sound directions in the input data is carried out in real-time by introducing delays between the left and right audio channels of the data and a sense of perceptual depth is created by changing the amplitudes of the input data. A delay between the two channels is created by using a buffer. The amplitude of the input data is changed by scaling the input data. The delay between channels and the amplitude scaling varies dynamically with time. The effective deployment of techniques showcased in this paper promises FPGA-based approaches in audio processing for spatial audio. The findings offer important perspectives that can inform further enhancements of FPGA-based spatial audio rendering in audio processing.

title: Real-time integrated CCTV using face and pedestrian detection image processing algorithm for automatic traffic light transitions
venue: 2015 International Conference on Humanoid, Nanotechnology, Information Technology,Communication and Control, Environment and Management (HNICEM)
abstract: With the technology today, detection of pedestrian was introduced to decrease the accidents in the roads. It was implemented on the traffic lights and cars. In this paper, integration of face detection and pedestrian takes place on the device called Raspberry Pi. OpenCV was used for the detections and programmed in Python. The webcam was used to capture images in real-time. The images was processed at the microprocessor. When pedestrians were detected, the microprocessor played the recorded voice and outputs it to the connecting speaker to notify those pedestrians or the pedestrian to wait before crossing until such time. The microprocessor sends a signal to the Gizduino to process the time of the red light's on state. The microcontroller was programmed with the traffic signals. When it receives a signal from the microprocessor, it added an extra seconds to the red light's on state. Afterwards, when it returned, it changed back to its original on state. The methods used for analyzing the data obtained were the Classification method and the Chi-square statistical test analysis. After testing, gathering data and computing each classification with the use of chi-square formula, the result of the success rate was 87.33% that showed that face and pedestrian detection that was integrated in the system successfully worked.

title: Real-Time IoT Monitoring of Battery Packs in EVs using Thermal Imaging and Edge AI Models
venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Inventive Computation Technologies (ICICT)
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) battery packs are susceptible to non-uniform heat which highly impacts safety, life, and energy efficiency. The traditional types of monitoring are based on point thermocouples that overlook localized hotspots and fast variation of temperatures. This paper presents an IoT-integrated thermal imaging system to detect potential anomalies in EV lithium-ion battery packs in real-time with the use of Edge AI models to map the temperature image accurately and measure the early signs of its potential development. An ESP32/Jetson Nano edge processor with a low-power FLIR Lepton 3.5 thermal sensor can be used to record high-resolution frames of temperature at 9Hz, and therefore can be used to do continuous monitoring without relying on the cloud. A thermal drift detection, hotspots, and abnormal temperature-rise prediction MobileNet CNN model is trained on an edge with a latency less than 80ms. The IoT dashboard is an MQTT system that delivers real-time temperature profiles, averaged temperature of the module, index of the hotspots zone and the forecasted thermal-runaway risk. When a 48 V EV battery module is loaded with drive-cycle loads and experimented, peak deviation of a hotspot is 12.6°C and 96.4 % of anomaly detection. The Communication overhead is also minimized 72 % with edge inference over cloud-based systems. This is a scalable, low-latency solution which can be deployed on two-wheelers, three-wheelers, and light electric vehicles to offer a safety-critical EV battery thermal health monitoring platform.

title: Real-time Lane Detection and Departure caution Gadget for Automobiles based on Raspberry pi
venue: 2023 International Conference on Advances in Electronics, Communication, Computing and Intelligent Information Systems (ICAECIS)
abstract: The advanced driver assistance machines critical aspect is lane detection (ADAS). even through several methologies have been put out via researches up so far, correctly detecting the street lanes below numerous environmental instances stays difficult trouble. The devices number one aim is to perceive lane departures to prevent injuries on the road and ensure pedestrain safety.To pick out and tune the road borders, cameras accumulated snapshots function as the devices number one entry. On raspberry pi hardware, the open CV library, the use of python is used to achive this concept of photograph processing this method can efficiently understand the roadways in a selection of tough occasions.

title: Real-time Linux in real time
venue: IBM Systems Journal
abstract: The increasing market demand for systems characterized by low-latency, deterministic behavior and the emphasis on the use of commodity hardware and software have led to a new breed of real-time operating systems (OSs), known as enterprise real-time OSs. In response to the demand for accelerated access to such features in a Linux™ kernel, the IBM Linux and Java™ Technology Centers collaborated to provide the first commercially available enterprise real-time Linux kernel with real-time Java support. Extending the PREEMPT RT patch from Ingo Molnar of Red Hat, Inc., the kernel contains additional features that were required to meet the demands of enterprise real-time OS customers. This paper describes how IBM developers helped to direct, implement, and test the real-time Linux kernel, bringing it from software patches to a finished product in nine months.

title: Real-time localization methodology with RFID technology in closed area
venue: 2017 25th Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU)
abstract: In recent years, many companies want to keep track of personnel, sources and working machines due to various reasons. This is sometimes achieved for security purposes and sometimes for coordination and performance purposes. The purpose and requirements are the main factors that determine the shape of tracking. Such developed systems for this purpose have different technologies according to their requirements. The real-time tracking can be determined with high precision in open areas with the global positioning system (GPS). However, previous research and developments for indoor tracking have mostly focused on infrared, wireless LAN and ultrasonic. In this study, the infrastructure of the system was designed by using RFID technology. The use of open source Geographical Information Systems (GIS) as a substructure also provided spatial display and analysis possibilities for this study. The open source t database is also integrated into this system. The tracking algorithm is completely unique and original and is encoded in the java programming language. In the algorithm, the accuracy of locating the proximity, direction and whether the RFID reader is on the right and left of the last point received is increased. The methodology used was tested in an underground salt mine and proved to study successfully.

title: Real-Time Monitoring and Performance Visualization of a Three-Phase Squirrel Cage Induction Motor
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Computing (ICONIC)
abstract: Three-phase squirrel cage motors show up everywhere in factories because they last long and work well. What you get here is a live tracking method with clear visuals, mixing physical tools and code smarts. From wires carrying power to spinning shaft speed, gadgets like voltage detectors, a current ring, and a little generator grab the numbers. That raw data - once just waves in circuits - turns sharp and readable through an ESP32 chip that speaks computer language. From there, the cleaned information heads into a computing setup. Inside, tools like Python plus MATLAB work out values including slip, torque, efficiency, power output, and power factor - also showing them in charts. Testing happened at Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology’s lab for machines. Results showed it runs well on the spot, proving it works in actual conditions.

title: Real-time monitoring portal for urban environment using sensor web technology
venue: 2010 18th International Conference on Geoinformatics
abstract: Taking advantage of the large-volume but low-cost datasets remotely sensed in urban areas by ubiquitous sensors or sensor networks, there is a need of real-time environmental monitoring portal or geospatial infrastructure for effectively or efficiently collecting and serving vast field data over web. Based on Open GIS Service Specifications defined by OGC Sensor Web Enablement (SWE), this paper presents an Internet based urban environment observation system that can real-time monitor environmental changes of temperature, humidity, illumination or air components in urban area. This system two functionality components. One is to collect and archive the environmental data from low-cost sensor network with user-customized time frequency through the proprietary system interfaces, the other is to support those datasets to be reformatted following Earth Observation (EO) specification and to be browsed or retrieved through the open interoperation interface of Sensor Observation Service (SOS). The real-time monitoring system is developed using Open GIS Specifications and Open Source Geospatial Software. The test-bed system is demonstrated as follows. The sensor kit deployed for constructing environmental monitoring network refers to the hardware implementation by GIS Research Group of OCU under Prof. Venkatesh. Currently, the factors of temperature, humidity, carbon dioxide and oxygen are sensed through outdoor sensors. The sensor data archive database is established using PostgreSQL and PostGIS platform and the web service system is run over Apache server. The data collection service and sensor data web service are programmed using Python, while the data visualization services are implemented using OpenLayers and Mapserver.

title: Real-Time Monitoring Technology for Sensitive Data Leakage Risk in Microservice APIs
venue: 2026 5th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology (ISCAIT)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of real-time monitoring and protection of sensitive data in the complex API call chains of microservice architectures. It proposes a real-time monitoring technology for sensitive data leakage risk targeting microservice APIs, aiming to establish a complete closed loop from fine-grained data perception to intelligent risk decision-making. The approach designs a lightweight tracing probe based on Java Agent bytecode enhancement, which constructs a real-time dynamic data flow spectrum through dynamic taint marking and cross-service label propagation. Furthermore, a Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) model, integrated with an attention mechanism, is proposed to model and quantify the risk of data flow sequences. Finally, an adaptive strategy response engine based on Deep Q-Learning (DQN) is introduced to dynamically optimize the alerting strategy. Experimental results show that the proposed system achieves precision, recall, and $\mathbf{F 1}$ scores of $88.7 \%, 91.3 \%$, and 89.9 %, respectively, and an $F 1$ score of 85.2% for detecting unknown anomalous traffic, significantly outperforming traditional rule-based and log-scanning methods. The system incurs low performance overhead with a resource consumption increase of less than 5 %, and an end-to-end processing delay of 210 milliseconds, demonstrating good stability and scalability. The proposed framework enables accurate, realtime, and adaptive monitoring of sensitive data leakage risks in microservice environments, with high production readiness.

title: Real-Time Moving Object Detection With Intruder Alert System for Enhanced Security
venue: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Computing, Information and Control Systems (ICOIICS)
abstract: Object detection has gained significant research interest in recent years due to its close connection with video analysis and image comprehension. Traditional approaches to object detection rely on handcrafted features and shallow trainable architectures. However, their performance tends to plateau, often requiring complex ensemble models that integrate multiple low-level image features with high-level contextual information from object detectors and scene classifiers. With advancements in deep learning, more sophisticated techniques capable of learning high-level semantic representations have emerged to overcome the limitations of traditional methods. These modern models differ in aspects such as network architecture, training strategies, and optimization functions. This paper presents Python-based object detection frameworks, highlighting key generic architectures and discussing modifications and techniques that enhance detection performance. Additionally, as different detection tasks possess unique characteristics, we briefly explore specialized applications such as salient object detection, face detection, and pedestrian detection. Furthermore, we provide experimental analyses comparing various methods and extracting insightful conclusions. Finally, we outline promising research directions and future challenges in object detection and deep learningbased recognition systems

title: Real-Time Multiplatform Emotion Classification Using CNN in a Fog Computing Environment
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: This paper introduces a robust multiplatform artificial intelligence (AI) system designed for real-time emotion classification in service robotics. The primary focus of this study is the development and implementation of an initial phase AI model within a diverse hardware ecosystem, enabling a Service Robot to interact dynamically with users in real-time, complemented by cloud connectivity and enhanced by fog computing techniques. Utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) via TensorFlow in Python, emotion classification models were crafted to discern various emotional states accurately. The AI system’s multiplatform environment comprised three distinct processing units: a laptop with Windows OS and high-end specifications, Jetson Orin running on a Linux architecture, and Raspberry Pi-4 operating on Raspbian OS. The inclusion of fog computing allowed for local data processing near the source, significantly reducing latency and ensuring faster response times, crucial for real-time applications. Training and comparative analysis were conducted on both the laptop and Jetson Orin, leveraging the GPU capabilities of each device. The Raspberry Pi-4 was allocated for monitoring and sensor data collection. Results revealed an impressive average performance of 90% in accurately classifying diverse emotional states. Training duration ranged from 20 minutes on the laptop to 30 minutes on Jetson Orin, with faster program execution observed on Jetson Orin due to its lightweight operating system. Cloud connectivity played a pivotal role in wirelessly monitoring, controlling, and facilitating real-time data collection. Additionally, it enabled the implementation of alert systems and notifications throughout the classification process. This pioneering approach lays a robust foundation for the advancement of sophisticated human-machine interaction systems, setting the stage for further research in the realm of AI-driven service robotics.

title: Real-Time Multiple Vehicle Counter using Background Subtraction for Traffic Monitoring System
venue: 2019 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Increasing population in an area of the world increasingly increases the density of the area. This is usually accompanied by an increase in vehicle volume resulting in congestion. Intelligent transportation systems (ITS) is one way to help the authorities in formulating rules and policies to deal with this problem, and can even automatically reduce congestion if it is integrated to regulate traffic lights. This research aims to build a traffic counter system in the city of Semarang, Indonesia. Traffic counter is one part of ITS which is tasked with calculating the volume of the vehicle by doing video processing obtained from the camera. The video used comes from a CCTV camera belonging to the Semarang city transportation office which can be accessed in real-time via a URL link. In the early stages of the construction of the system, videos from CCTV were installed in the Tugu Muda area. Tugu Muda is one of the most densely packed streets in the city of Semarang and it should be noted that this area has a form that is quite complicated because it has an intersection that connects five main streets. The video processing uses the background subtraction method, binary threshold, morphology, detecting object using contour, and tracking objects to calculate vehicle volume. This system generates vehicle volume reports that can be accessed directly in real-time with web-based applications built with Python programming languages with OpenCV editors. To test the accuracy of the traffic counter system calculation is done by comparing manual calculations with system calculations on several video samples taken from different times, namely in the morning time, day time and afternoon.

title: Real-Time News Aggregation and Sentiment Analysis Using Web Scraping and Firebase Integration
venue: 2025 9th International Conference on Inventive Systems and Control (ICISC)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time news aggregation and sentiment analysis platform that offers users sentiment-classified news headlines. The system uses the method of web scraping for getting news headlines from online sources on an hourly basis. Then after the headlines are collected, the sentiment of each one is analyzed by the VADER that is a part of NLTK of Python. It classifies them as negative, neutral, or positive. The whole process involves the data that are sent to Firebase for storage. This technology has got the advantage of scalability and reliability. The mobile application client version is characterized with a simple navigation facility, interactive screen and sentiment tab for news of various categories. The interface of the client-side app is simple and neat, and apart from the usual login, it allows sentiment-based news tabs to IT users. The practical assessment of the sentiment analysis by means of this component is proved to have a high degree of credibility in different news categories and we observe the level of satisfaction across these categories and for a large proportion of the population. The demonstration is based not only on the high processing speed at the cost of running out of training data, learning time, or direct control over the problems to be solved, but also on the minimum distance between the output of those said methods of analysis and the user's request. Results from the interviews reveal that the system is spot-on in the way it allows people to filter the news according to the sentiment they are looking for. The result provides the system with room for further improvement, such as the use of more advanced sentiment analysis techniques and the extension of the application to add other features.

title: Real-Time Nurse Dispatching Using Dynamic Priority Decision Framework
venue: 2020 Winter Simulation Conference (WSC)
abstract: The increase in medical treatment complexity can cause experienced nurses to have difficulty determining priorities among patient needs. Electronic health record systems will enable automated decision support to assist medical professionals in making these determinations. This article details a framework that uses a discrete-event simulation, programmed in Python, to determine how priorities should be assigned in real time based on characteristics of patient needs. The severity of patient needs is dynamic because severity increases over time until the need is addressed. The simulation framework is applied to a cardiac care unit with 14 patients, who collectively have 125 needs. Four different priority schemes are evaluated and their effectiveness compared under the assumption of an 8 or 9 nurse capacity. The results illustrate the importance of modeling the dispatching of nurses according to severity because, although fewer nurses result in longer average queue times, they can handle higher-severity needs effectively.

title: Real-Time Object and Personnel Tracking in Indoor Location
venue: 2019 4th International Conference on Computer Science and Engineering (UBMK)
abstract: The low efficiency of GPS technology in indoor environments enables the development of wireless media technologies such as WLAN, RFID, UWB and BLE in these environments. Given the cost and accuracy of these systems, BLE technology is low in cost and easy to locate in the environment. However, accuracy is lower in server-based systems. In order to solve this problem, the system we propose is based on filtering the data, performing RSSI-distance estimation and estimating the position using WCL algorithm. In the system, positions were obtained with an average error of 0.5 m near the gateway, 2.42 m between the gateways and 2.29 m in the middle of the plan.

title: Real-Time Object Size Dimensioning in Raspberry Pi
venue: 2022 7th International Conference on Communication and Electronics Systems (ICCES)
abstract: Real-time object size dimensioning and detection is playing a crucial part in industry today and in the coming days of technological advancement. Object Size Dimensioning is a framework for estimating the dimensions i.e., length and breadth of real-time objects. To demonstrate the efficiency of the suggested system, the demonstration has been implemented and shown in Raspberry Pi. The proposed approach includes an item or object that is identified using improved techniques for detecting edges. For calculating dimension, a reference item (a binary coded marker) has been taken based on characteristics that items used as reference can be identified easily and have fixed measurements. This model has been proposed using the Open CV python module in Raspberry Pi, for determining the dimensioning of an object using a fixed reference.

title: Real-Time OCR and Translation System with Text-to-Speech Ability
venue: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The demand for the seamless cross-linguistic interaction has heightened with increasingly high globalization and digital connectivity, particularly in contexts where real-time interaction is required. This paper aspires to address the development of an integrated Optical Character Recognition system, translation, and Text-to-Speech system in behalf of these demands. The proposed system uses OpenCV for video capture, Tesseract for multilingual OCR citeMishra2022, Google Translate API for translation, and gTTS for audio output. This approach offers an adaptive and flexible accessibility solution in educational and multilingual interactions. The language switch is done dynamically, thus giving the user flexibility to change the language of choice in real-time so that it becomes a very flexible and all-inclusive environment. The design of this system went through three iterations that continue to improve with respect to the accuracy of outcomes, efficiency of processing, and usability. Results have indicated that the system is quite efficient in its application, making high accuracy for OCR, reliable translations, and clear audio outputs-applicable in real-world applications. Future improvements will be made in increasing language support, latency reduction, along with other features of accessibility to enhance inclusivity and engagement.

title: Real-Time Oscillation Analytics for Power Grids: A Wavelet-Assisted Matrix Pencil Approach in SLDC Operations
venue: 2025 11th International Conference on Power Systems (ICPS)
abstract: Low-frequency oscillations in the 0.1–3 Hz range are frequently observed in power systems and pose a risk to grid stability if not identified in time. This work presents a lightweight real-time analytics tool developed in Python and Streamlit for Telangana SLDC. The tool employs wavelet analysis to identify oscillation periods, followed by the Matrix Pencil Method (MPM) to estimate frequency, damping, and mode shapes. FFT is also used as a quick validation step. The tool was tested with real PMU data, and two case studies are discussed: a 1.49 Hz forced oscillation due to a turbine controller fault, and a 1.84 Hz natural oscillation during a line outage at a hydel station. The results show that the proposed hybrid FFT + wavelet–MPM approach provides more accurate information and allows SLDC operators to take corrective action in a timely manner.

title: Real-Time Pain Detection using Facial Expression Analysis and Transfer Learning
venue: 2026 International Conference on Visual Analytics and Data Visualization (ICVADV)
abstract: This project addresses the critical challenge of objective pain assessment by developing a real-time, non-invasive system for Pain Detection exclusively using Facial Expression Analysis. Traditional pain monitoring relies on subjective selfreport, which is unreliable when patients are non-communicative or masking their condition. The method involves a low-cost data acquisition setup where facial expressions were captured by a webcam and precisely synchronized with 'Normal'/'Pain' markers using the Lab Streaming Layer (LSL) protocol. The combined data was stored in XDF files. A custom Python pipeline was developed to process these files: first extracting and labeling over 15,000 face images (resized to $224 \times 224$ pixels) based on the LSL markers. The core of the system is a Transfer Learning model built on MobileNetV2, which was trained in a two-phase process to classify facial cues into 'Pain' or 'Normal' states. Results acquired on the validation set demonstrated a classification accuracy of 79 %, with a robust Pain Precision of 85 %, significantly reducing the number of false alarms in a clinical context. The system provides a highly reliable, objective, and deployable metric for pain, enhancing clinical monitoring and supporting improved patient care.

title: Real-time path planning of factory car based on image processing and Dijkstra algorithm
venue: 2nd International Conference on Mechatronic Automation and Electrical Engineering (ICMAEE 2024)
abstract: Tracking cars are widely used in factories. However, there are relatively big limitations to tracking cars. The tracking cars can only walk according to the line drawn in the factory and cannot find the shortest distance between two points, which leads to a reduction in efficiency. To solve the phenomenon of frequent detours sometimes appearing in tracking cars, a solution is designed in this paper. In the case of the obvious gray level difference between the factory floor and the obstacles. A camera is used on the ceiling of the factory to take pictures at regular intervals and then pass the photos to the local segment of the computer. The Python program automatically reads the pictures and processes the pictures using the Canny operator. After processing by the Canny operator, the Dijkstra algorithm is used to design the shortest path between the starting position and the ending position of the car in this paper. In this way, a method to find the shortest path is finally obtained. After obtaining the shortest path for automatic cars, TCP/IP is used to transmit the planned path to the cars. This research can greatly improve the working efficiency of the car in the factory.

title: Real-Time Phasor Estimation via the Taylor-Fourier's Subspace
venue: 2018 North American Power Symposium (NAPS)
abstract: This paper focuses on the real-time phasor estimation via Taylor-Fourier’s Subspace (TFS) on a low-cost embedded platform. Signal processing is carried out using a sliding window for the sampled signal by the Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC). A digital Taylor-Fourier filter designed using the TFS, deals with the extraction of the dynamic phasor estimates such as: amplitude, phase angle, frequency, and rate of change of frequency (ROCOF). Then, a Python-based interface is developed to display the real-time monitoring for those parameters. Finally, results exhibit the performance of the implemented phasor estimator attaining reliable estimates for both simulated and real signals, and tracking accurately the changes in amplitude, phase and frequency.

title: Real-Time Pipe Burst Localization in Water Distribution Networks Using Change Point Detection Algorithms
venue: 2024 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Networks and Computer Communications (ETNCC)
abstract: Change point detection (CPD) has proved to be an effective tool for detecting drifts in data and its use over the years has become more pronounced due to the vast amount of data and IoT devices readily available. This study analyzes the effectiveness of Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) and Shewhart Control Charts for identifying the occurrence of abrupt pressure changes for pipe burst localization in Water Distribution Network (WDN). Change point detection algorithms could be useful for identifying the nodes that register the earliest and most drastic pressure changes with the aim of detecting pipe bursts in real-time. TSN et, a Python package, is employed in order to simulate pipe bursts in a WDN. The pressure readings are served to the pipe burst localization algorithm the moment they are available for real-time pie burst localization. The performance of the pipe burst localization algorithm is evaluated using a key metric such as localization accuracy under different settings to compare its performance when paired with either CUSUM or Shewhart. Results show that the pipe burst localization algorithm has an overall better performance when paired with CUSUM. Although, it does show great accuracy for both CPD algorithms when pressure readings are being continuously made available without a big gap between time steps. The proposed approach however still needs further experiments on different WDNs to assess the performance and accuracy of the algorithm on real-world WDN models.

title: Real-Time Port Scan Detection and Automated Response Framework Using Log-Based Analysis and SIEM Integration
venue: 2026 Third International Conference on Networking and Communications (ICNWC)
abstract: Port scanning is one of the most commonly used techniques by attackers to identify vulnerable services within a target network. Detecting such activities at an early stage is essential to prevent further intrusion attempts. This paper presents a real-time port scan detection and automated response framework that integrates log-based network traffic analysis with Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) capabilities using Splunk. The proposed system uses a Python-based detection engine to continuously analyse network events and identify malicious scanning behaviour based on temporal patterns and abnormal port access activities. Detected scan events are recorded in a structured format and forwarded to Splunk, where centralized indexing, correlation, visualization, and alerting are performed. Additionally, the framework supports an automated firewall mechanism that dynamically blocks malicious source IP addresses, creating a closed-loop detection and response system. Security teams can monitor, analyse, and investigate scanning incidents in real time through Splunk dashboards and correlation rules. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves a high detection rate with low response time, while also providing improved visibility and scalability through SIEM integration. This framework can be effectively deployed in enterprise environments and Security Operations Centre (SOCs) to strengthen proactive, data-driven network defence

title: Real-Time Posture Correction using MediaPipe
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Intelligent Communication Technologies and Virtual Mobile Networks (ICICV)
abstract: This project aims to tackle the issue of corrections and lack of repetition in the face of the home exercise without having a human trainer to check the posture of the exercise. Squats, push-ups and bicep curls are some of the exercises that many people carry out poorly, resulting in low effectiveness and possible injuries. The available fitness programs do not necessarily have automatic performance evaluation and real-time corrections of forms. In order to address these constraints, the proposed system would support an intelligent camera-based virtual trainer which could identify the wrong postures, register the repetitions and provide live corrective feedback; thus, facilitating safe and effective self training exercises. It is a Python project utilizing MediaPipe BlazePose to identify 33 body key points parts in live video streams. It measures the joint angles to determine real time movements, categorizes the stages of an exercise and determines accuracy of the form. It has a modular design that is shaped to suit various exercises and skill levels. The Streamlit interface has real-time feedback, automatic tally of rep, posture correct and historical data of daily exercise, and progress tracking. Three main exercises were put to test on this project and they included bicep curls, squats, and pushups. The model is highly accurate and reliable with accurateity of 96% and precision of 97%, recall of 97%, and F1-score of 97% in case of bicep curls. In the case of squats, it achieved a 97% accuracy, 98% precision, 98% recall and F1-score of 98%. With push-ups, it had an accuracy of 96% at 95% precision, a recall of 97% and an F1-score of 96% which means that the performance was slightly worse since the patterns of motion used are more complex. In general, the findings confirm that the system can be used as an efficient AI-powered fitness assistant that should be capable of providing a consistent and precise exercise tracking, which will allow one to adopt scalable, pos

title: Real-Time Predictive Control for Energy Self-Sufficiency in PV-Battery Microgrids with Bidirectional Electric Vehicle Integration
venue: IECON 2025 – 51st Annual Conference of the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society
abstract: This paper presents a real-time predictive control strategy aimed at maximizing energy self-sufficiency in an industrial microgrid integrating photovoltaic (PV) generation, lithium-ion battery storage, and bidirectional electric vehicles, using the paradigm of Vehicle to Grid (V2G). The proposed Economic Model Predictive Control (EMPC) framework leverages forecasts of solar production, load demand, and vehicle availability to optimize energy flows over a prediction horizon. The control architecture relies on a real-time implementation using industrial-grade hardware, with a layered structure combining a programmable logic controller (PLC) and a Python-based optimization environment. The system is experimentally validated on a testbench equipped with real power converters and programmable loads. Results demonstrate that the integration of V2G enhances the flexibility and autonomy of the microgrid, enabling reduced dependence on the external grid and improved use of renewable resources. The proposed approach contributes to the development of resilient and intelligent energy systems for industrial applications.

title: Real-time programming with Java technologies
venue: Fourth IEEE International Symposium on Object-Oriented Real-Time Distributed Computing. ISORC 2001
abstract: The Java programming language brings different benefits to different audiences. The article examines common perspectives on what Java offers, or ought to offer to the domain of real time programming. It is concluded that real time programming with Java technologies is a reality today. Emerging technologies will increase the breadth of options available to real time programmers who choose to build on the Java platform. Each real time technology enables slightly different benefits and exposes different risks. Real time developers should familiarize themselves with the alternative approaches before committing to a particular technology.

title: Real-Time Radio Refractivity Estimation Using the Differentiable Split-Step Fourier Parabolic Equation
venue: 2025 Photonics & Electromagnetics Research Symposium - Spring (PIERS-Spring)
abstract: A functional minimization problem with respect to the refractive index is posed. The functional to be minimized compares the solution to the forward problem with measured electromagnetic field data at the receivers. The forward problem is solved using the split-step Fourier method for the parabolic wave equation. This method is represented as a computational graph. By applying the automatic differentiation method to the computational graph, the gradient of the objective functional with respect to the refractive index can be efficiently computed. This gradient is used to find the optimal solution. The refractive index is represented as a multilayer perceptron. The proposed method is implemented in Python 3 using the JAX automatic differentiation framework. Unlike the variational adjoint approach, proposed method computes the gradient directly from the numerical scheme code, eliminating the need for a separate solution of the adjoint equation. Numerical experiments were conducted for typical refractive index profiles and irregular terrain. It was shown that the proposed method can be used for real-time tracking of variations in the tropospheric refractive index.

title: Real-time reasoning: the case of surveillance systems
venue: 2005 IEEE Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation
abstract: The paper presents a layered architecture for real-time surveillance systems. Each layer includes objects that model the "real world" at a specific abstraction level, from raw data up to domain concepts. Each layer performs abstractions on perceptions coming from the lower layer and formulates timed hypotheses about domain objects. The failure of a hypothesis causes a perception to flow up-stream. In turn, hypotheses flow down-stream, so that their verification is delegated to the lower layers. The proposed architectural patterns have been reified in a Java framework, which has been used in an experimental multi-camera tracking system.

title: Real-time remote attestation of IaaS cloud
venue: 2012 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Cloud Computing and Intelligence Systems
abstract: Aiming at the deficiencies when deploying existing remote attestation approaches in the IaaS cloud, this paper proposes a real-time remote attestation approach for IaaS cloud. The approach includes a realtime remote attestation architecture and corresponding dynamic measurement mechanism and reference generation mechanism. The contributions can be concluded into three aspects. Firstly, it alleviates the TOCTOU (Time of Check, Time of Use) problem. Secondly the load of verification is low, as makes it acceptable for thin clients. Thirdly the runtime behavior of the software is measured dynamically. In our prototype it is shown that the approach can detect the attacks such as code injection.

title: Real-Time Roadside Animal Detection for Traffic Safety Using Yolov8 and Faster RCNN
venue: 2025 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Roadside animal detection systems are advancing road safety by integrating real-time animal detection into traffic monitoring and in-vehicle applications. This scalable, softwareonly solution can be deployed on personal computers or servers, offering an efficient way to prevent vehicle-animal collisions. Using deep learning, this system leverages advanced object detection models like YOLO (You Only Look Once) and Faster R-CNN, achieving accurate animal detection from live video feeds captured by roadside or in-vehicle cameras. The system is built entirely in Python and uses frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch for developing detection models, while OpenCV facilitates real-time video processing. By identifying and classifying animals, the system displays bounding boxes with confidence scores around detected animals, providing clear visual cues to drivers. Its primary goal is to deliver timely alerts, helping to minimize vehicle collisions with wildlife, especially in areas with frequent wildlife crossings. Designed to be robust, the system operates effectively under a range of environmental conditions, ensuring reliable detection during both day and night. This project ultimately aims to enhance road safety and reduce the environmental impact of vehicle-wildlife collisions, addressing a pressing need for sustainable and intelligent traffic solutions.

title: Real-Time Route Simulation Using Offline Data and Dijkstra's Algorithm
venue: 2026 International Conference on Computational Robotics, Testing and Engineering Evaluation (ICCRTEE)
abstract: Real-time navigation in areas of limited or nonexistent internet access, such as crisis zones, remote areas and areas affected by disasters, can pose a challenge. The system can also be interpreted as a global path planning framework for autonomous robotic navigation in GPS-denied environments. A Lightweight, fully offline Navigation System (W-NAV), built using open-source tools such as OpenStreetMap, Leaflet.js, Folium, and a local Python HTTP Server, is presented herein as an appropriate solution to this need. W-NAV allows users to navigate, zoom, pan and visualize animated routes in a predefined map area (which can be preloaded using locally stored OpenStreetMap data) without an active Internet connection (Wi-Fi or cellular). Users can navigate the geographic area of their choice, and therefore utilize previously established (POIs), such as hospitals or shelters, at the same level of functionality available on contemporary laptops and/or mobile devices utilizing accurate location information from a Wi-Fi or cellular connection. Furthermore, users can access POIs even if those areas have minimal (low-income) resources. Thus, the system achieves approximately 98% routing accuracy using preloaded OpenStreetMap data. The modular architecture of W-NAV supports ongoing development and enhancement capabilities such as: GPS integration; offline search capabilities; hazard mapping overlays; and mapping layers related to specific crises. The W-NAV framework serves as an extremely valuable resource to aid the development of local and regional humanitarian efforts, disaster response teams, and the governing body of an area in both rural and urban environments. Additionally, the framework supports autonomous robotic navigation in GPS-denied environments by enabling precomputed routes as global path plans and facilitating integration with sensor-based localization.

title: Real-Time Semantic Background Subtraction
venue: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
abstract: Semantic background subtraction (SBS) has been shown to improve the performance of most background subtraction algorithms by combining them with semantic information, derived from a semantic segmentation network. However, SBS requires high-quality semantic segmentation masks for all frames, which are slow to compute. In addition, most state-of-the-art background subtraction algorithms are not real-time, which makes them unsuitable for real-world applications. In this paper, we present a novel background subtraction algorithm called Real-Time Semantic Background Subtraction (denoted RT-SBS) which extends SBS for real-time constrained applications while keeping similar performances. RT-SBS effectively combines a real-time background subtraction algorithm with high-quality semantic information which can be provided at a slower pace, independently for each pixel. We show that RT-SBS coupled with ViBe sets a new state of the art for real-time background subtraction algorithms and even competes with the non real-time state-of-the-art ones. Note that we provide python CPU and GPU implementations of RT-SBS at https://github.com/cioppaanthony/rt-sbs.

title: Real-Time Sign Language Converter for Mute and Deaf People
venue: 2021 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Vision (AIMV)
abstract: Deaf people may get irritated due to the problem of not being able to share their views with common people, which may affect their day-to-day life. This is the main reason to develop such system that can help these people and they can also put their thoughts forward similar to other people who don’t have such problem. The advancement in the Artificial intelligence provides the door for developing the system that overcome this difficulty. So this project aims on developing a system which will be able to convert the speech to text for the deaf person, and also sometimes the person might not be able to understand just by text, so the speech will also get converted to the universal sign language. Similarly, for the mute people the sign language which they are using will get converted to speech. We will take help of various ML and AI concepts along with NLP to develop the accurate model. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) will be used for prediction as it is efficient in predicting image input, also as lip movements are fast and continuous so it is hard to capture so along with CNN, the use of attention-based long short-term memory (LSTM) will prove to be efficient. Data Augmentation methods will be used for getting the better results. TensorFlow and Keras are the python libraries that will be used to convert the speech to text. Currently there are many software available but all requires the network connectivity for it to work, while this device will work without the requirement of internet.Using the proposed model we got the accuracy of 100% in predicting sign language and 96% accuracy in sentence level understanding.

title: Real-Time Sign Language Detection
venue: 2023 2nd International Conference on Vision Towards Emerging Trends in Communication and Networking Technologies (ViTECoN)
abstract: Lack of communication or miscommunication brought on by linguistic problems can lead to awkward situations in today's culture. Those who are deaf or have trouble hearing use sign language, a visual form of communication, to communicate. It communicates meaning through hand gestures and body language. Yet not everyone is able to interpret sign language, which might result in miscommunication. A system was developed employing cutting-edge technologies to address this problem, including deep learning, machine learning, convolutional neural networks, computer vision, TensorFlow, and Python. This technology is made to accurately detect and identify sign language motions in real-time. The system develops a real-time sign language recognition tool using OpenCV. The 26 letters in American Sign were categorised using a CNN classifier. The use of technology to bridge communication gaps and create inclusive environments is crucial in our society. This system's high accuracy rate is an excellent indication of its reliability, providing a promising solution for individuals who use sign language to communicate. It would be interesting to learn more about the specific CNN classifier used in the project and how it was trained to recognize ASL gestures. Overall, the implementation of this technology can create more inclusive and accessible environments, ensuring that everyone can communicate effectively, regardless of their abilities or differences.

title: Real-Time Sign Language Recognition and Communication: Leveraging CNN for Deaf and Mute Communities
venue: 2024 International Conference on Innovation and Novelty in Engineering and Technology (INNOVA)
abstract: Accessibility, communication, and empowerment issues are common for people with sensory disabilities. Although this problem has been the subject of many studies, there is no one-stop application. The accessibility platform is a platform-independent application accessible through a website. This initiative seeks to assist in resolving these issues through the real-time translation of Indian sign language into text. Additionally, it would provide users the opportunity to connect with NGOs that focus on empowering people with disabilities. It is web-based making it platform-independent. The system aims to create a comprehensive, all-in-one feature platform, rather than focusing on individual features. The Indian Sign Language feature uses a Convolutional Neural Network as the algorithm for image classification, it uses Leaky ReLu and Adams optimizers. The use of these optimizers ensures that the accuracy of the research reaches above 90 percent in comparison to the accuracy of other networks that use sigmoid and tanh activation functions. The system achieved an accuracy of 97 percent in real time with the data set of 1200 images and 35 classes i.e. 26 alphabets and 9 numbers.

title: Real-Time Sign Language Recognition for Enhanced Communication
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Internet of Things: Smart Innovation and Usages (IoT-SIU)
abstract: Real-Time Sign Language Recognition (RTSLG) employs technology to turn hand signals into speech or text. This helps people who are deaf and people who can hear talk to each other. Even while hand signals are great for sending complicated messages, it’s still hard to understand these quick movements in real time. Current sign language recognition systems generally have trouble understanding gestures that change over time and make mistakes when the lighting changes in the backdrop, which makes them less useful overall. We created a cutting-edge Real-Time Sign Language Gesture (RTSLG) system using a sophisticated deep learning framework that includes Python, TensorFlow, OpenCV, and Keras to get around these problems. We use Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in our method to get precise picture detection and computer vision processing of hand movements that recording devices pick up. The proposed system demonstrated an impressive accuracy rate of $95 \%$ in recognizing and converting gestures into text, offering a robust and efficient solution for improving communication between deaf and hearing individuals.

title: Real-Time Sign Language Recognition System with Web-Scraped Datasets and Image Annotation for Accessibility and Human-Computer Interaction Applications
venue: 2026 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
abstract: This paper proposed the methodology for developing a real-time sign language recognition system using web-scraped datasets and image annotation through Roboflow. Models like CNN and RetinaNet were trained using Python frameworks, and text-to-speech tools translated gestures into native and English languages. The system is deployed as a Streamlit-based web application with robust security measures to protect user data. The system provides high accuracy in gesture classes, low latency, and high throughput. This application can be given to the accessibility and human-computer interaction application.

title: Real-time Sign Language Translation Using LSTM
venue: 2025 11th International Conference on Smart Computing and Communications (ICSCC)
abstract: This paper concerns a real-time sign language translating system that employs long short term memory (LSTM) neural networks for accurate recognition and understanding of gestures. The system is based on video feeds of hand gestures. Then these gestures are translated to meaningful text that could help in communication between hearingimpaired people. The system has been developed using the various programming languages- Python, Tensorflow, OpenCV, and NumPy and posses merits like being highly accurate and real-time and quite user-friendly. The system also supports dynamic growing datasets and thus can be customized to various sign languages. This scalable solution can be applied in education, healthcare, and contribution toward social integration because it bridges communication gaps between people through assistive deep learning technology.

title: Real-Time Sign Language-to-Speech Translation System With AI-Powered Wearable Technology
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Globally, over 430 million people live with disabling hearing loss, a number projected to rise to 2.5 billion by 2050 according to the World Health Organization. Among them, individuals with mutism or profound hearing impairments often rely on sign language as their primary mode of communication. However, a communication gap persists, as most people in the general population are not proficient in sign language. This barrier hampers inclusion, access to services, and full societal participation for individuals with hearing and speech disabilities. To address this challenge, we present SignSpeak, a real-time cyber-physical system that translates sign language gestures into audible speech, enabling interactions between sign language users and non-signers. The system features a wearable glove embedded with flex sensors on each finger and a spatial sensor for wrist tracking. Data from these sensors is collected by an Arduino microcontroller and processed using machine learning models implemented in Python and TensorFlow to recognize and classify gestures accurately. The recognized gestures are then converted into synthesized speech output. By combining low-cost hardware with scalable software, SignSpeak offers an affordable, portable, and user-friendly solution to bridge the communication divide. We evaluate the system in terms of recognition accuracy, responsiveness, and practicality, demonstrating its potential to support real-time communication in educational, professional, and social contexts. Experimental validation confirmed that SignSpeak achieved an average recognition accuracy of 94.7% across 29 gesture classes, including alphabet letters and basic expressions, with an end-to-end response time of 112 ms. These results demonstrate both reliability and real-time usability, reinforcing the potential of the proposed solution as an accessible communication aid.

title: Real-time simulation in Java: A feasibility study
venue: 2008 Asia Simulation Conference - 7th International Conference on System Simulation and Scientific Computing
abstract: Massively multiplayer online human in the loop simulation (MMOHILS) is a novel simulation technique which borrows heavily from the field of gaming. This naturally raises the question: is a general-purpose programming language such as Java (which has been used to program games) suitable for implementing a MMOHILS? Our work shows that, yes, Java can meet the demands of a real-time, multiple-man-in-the-loop simulation.

title: Real-time single channel EEG motor imagery based Brain Computer Interface
venue: 2016 World Automation Congress (WAC)
abstract: This paper presents a motor imagery based Brain Computer Interface (BCI) that uses single channel EEG signal from the C3 or C4 electrode placed in the motor area of the head. Time frequency analysis using Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT) is used to compute spectrogram from the EEG data. The STFT is scaled to have gray level values on which Grey Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) is computed. Texture descriptors such as correlation, energy, contrast, homogeneity and dissimilarity are calculated from the GLCM matrices. The texture descriptors are used to train a logistic regression classifier which is then used to classify the left and right motor imagery signals. The single-channel motor imagery classification system is tested offline with different subjects. The average offline accuracy is 87.6%. An online BCI system is implemented in openViBE with the single channel classification scheme. The stimuli presentations and feedback are implemented in Python and integrated with the openViBe BCI system.

title: Real-Time Sonar Image Simulation for Adaptive Template Matching in Automatic Target Recognition
venue: IEEE Journal of Oceanic Engineering
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) equipped with side-looking sonars have become vital tools for seafloor exploration due to the combination of high image resolution and high area coverage rates. To reach their full operational performance AUVs also need onboard perception, including recognition of relevant objects. We combine adaptive template matching and real-time image simulation for automatic target recognition in synthetic aperture sonar images. We hypothesize that dynamic, rapid and fine-tuned search of object types and configurations should improve classification results and real-time responses. Analyses of experimental data with cylindrical objects outside of Horten, Norway, recorded by the Kongsberg Maritime HISAS1030 sonar, strengthened the hypothesis. Our setup outperformed a well-configured, static template database at false positive rates (FPR) above 10%–20%, with an area under curve improvement of one to two percent, depending on the correlation methods used. The system is implemented on a graphics processing unit using OpenGL and OpenCL, a computer graphics and general-purpose programming library, respectively. This facilitates a faster and more flexible classification process. We describe the implementation and provide a supplementary Python script to showcase the notation and implementation in practice.

title: Real-Time Speech Emotion Recognition using LSTM
venue: 2026 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is a task of emotion identification in speech signals to enable machines to communicate in a more natural and meaningful way. In this paper, we proposed a real-time SER system based on a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model. The proposed system uses Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) to extract relevant features from the speech signal that represent emotional patterns. The features are then used as input to the LSTM model for emotion classification such as happy, sad, angry, and neutral. The use of TensorFlow and Python in the system makes it capable of achieving real-time performance with the features of smooth prediction and high accuracy. The research focuses on the emotional intelligence advancement of AI applications such as healthcare monitoring and virtual assistants.

title: Real-Time Speech-to-Speech Translator: Analysis and Implementation
venue: 2025 4th International Conference on Distributed Computing and Electrical Circuits and Electronics (ICDCECE)
abstract: Speech-to-speech translation (S2ST) technology bridges language barriers, enabling seamless communication across cultures. This paper presents a modular system integrating Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Machine Translation (MT), and Text-to-Speech (TTS) for real-time translation. Leveraging Python, Google APIs, and self-supervised models, the system achieves high accuracy (ASR: 90– 95%, MT: 85–90%) and low latency (2–3 seconds). Key contributions include noise filtering, scalable architecture, and support for low-resource languages. Applications span healthcare, education, and global collaboration, emphasizing the practical significance of this innovation.

title: Real-Time Sports Analytics System: A Low Cost Single Camera Football Analysis Pipeline
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Future Innovations (ETFI)
abstract: Post-match analytics in association football helps coaches and analysts quantify performance, identify tactical patterns, and validate qualitative observations. However, many commercial systems rely on multi-camera infrastructure, proprietary sensors, or expensive subscriptions. This paper presents the Real-Time Football Analytics System (RTFAS), a low-cost single-camera analytics pipeline built with opensource Python tooling (OpenCV, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, NetworkX). Given a recorded match video, RTFAS estimates a camera-to-pitch homography, tracks players across frames via lightweight multi-object tracking, assigns team labels using jersey-color clustering, infers possession and pass/shot events using spatio-temporal heuristics, and generates coach-ready reports including heatmaps, formation maps, passing networks, shot charts, and possession timelines. The design prioritizes deployability on commodity CPU hardware while remaining extensible to learned components (re-identification and data-driven expected-goals models).

title: Real-Time Stability Analysis of PI and PID Controllers for Bicopter Roll Motion Control
venue: 2026 International Conference on Circuit, Systems and Communication (ICCSC)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) require effective control systems to ensure stable flight under external disturbances. This paper evaluates the real-time performance of PI and PID controllers for bicopter roll motion stabilization. The controller gains were determined using the Ziegler-Nichols autotuning method, and the system was implemented in real time using a Python Graphical User Interface (GUI) and an ESP32 microcontroller to regulate motor speeds through pulse-width modulation (PWM) signals. Experimental tests were carried out under external perturbations, and the roll angle response was analyzed using rise time, overshoot, settling time, and steady-state error. The experimental results show that the PI controller achieved stable roll regulation within a steady-state error range of (±3°), but with higher overshoot and longer settling time. In comparison, the PID controller improved the transient response and reduced overshoot and settling time. In particular, the PID controller with $K_{d}=0.4$ provided the best balance between fast stabilization and damping without introducing oscillations. However, increasing the derivative gain to $K_{d}=0.8$ produced oscillatory behavior and reduced stability. Overall, the PID controller demonstrated superior performance for real-time bicopter roll stabilization under identical disturbance conditions.

title: Real-Time Surface Type Recognition on Airport Runways Using YOLOv8 with Semantic Segmentation
venue: 2025 Signal Processing: Algorithms, Architectures, Arrangements, and Applications (SPA)
abstract: This paper presents the development and evaluation of a vision-based system for automatic surface type recognition on airport runways using the YOLOv8 object detection algorithm. The proposed system was trained to identify four surface classes— concrete, asphalt, grass, and paving stones—from video data recorded during vehicle traversals of an airfield. Several YOLOv8 variants, including standard and segmentation-based models (YOLOv8n, s, m and YOLOv8n-seg, s-seg, m-seg), were implemented and compared in terms of performance metrics such as mAP, inference speed, and detection confidence. A custom dataset of over 600 augmented images was created using the Roboflow platform, allowing for diverse training conditions. A Python-based bilingual GUI was developed for model selection, video processing, and CSV export of detection results. Experimental results show that YOLOv8n-seg achieves the best balance between detection precision and computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time deployment in low-resource environments.

title: Real-Time Surveillance for Identification of Fruits Ripening Stages and Vegetables Maturation Stages with Infection Detection
venue: 2021 6th International Conference on Signal Processing, Computing and Control (ISPCC)
abstract: For every fruit and vegetable, there are various ripening stages and maturation stages. For example, according to US standards for greenhouse tomatoes, there are six stages in tomato ripening. But the useful stages are only last two. Improper supervision in harvest methods and fertilization leads to the decrease in the post-harvest life of fruit and vegetables. Monitoring the ripening stages and maturation stages require proper knowledge of color and size of fruits and vegetables. In order to decrease excessive labor charges and wastages of fruits and vegetables, autonomous farming methods can be introduced. In autonomous farming, the main objective is to detect a vegetable or a fruit is ripe or not and it’s infected or not. If this objective is achieved then farmers can easily harvest fruits and remove the infected fruits too. The infected fruits need to be removed so that it doesn’t infect others. And proper fertilizers can be given to there to fruits. For example, if mango is infected by a deficiency disease then proper vitamin fertilizer can be given to the fruit. So by using image processing in python using an efficient HSL color space algorithm and OpenCV library,a real time monitoring system is made to identify the maturation and ripening stages of a vegetable or fruit and to check whether a fruit is infected or not. Based on the comparison of existing systems for various fruits and vegetables, there is a very scarce availability for some fruits and vegetables detection of stages, which specifically in real time image processing. By using images there are lot of disadvantages where we need to take a lot of pictures, the lighting, and in real time in farming it is tedious. So live detection of image processing is done in the proposed system using Open CV library in python. In existing system RGB color spaces are used. Here an efficient algorithm using HSL color space is used to identify a fruit vegetable ripening and maturation stages. The proposed system also

title: Real-time text recognition and text-to-speech processing system for visually impaired
