venue: 4th International Conference on Distributed Sensing and Intelligent Systems (ICDSIS 2023)
abstract: In contemporary society, the pace of our daily lives has reached such a level of intensity that we find ourselves with limited opportunities to engage with crucial informational resources. The act of reading has transitioned from being obligatory to becoming elective. The preference for podcasts over novels and other written media is driven by the perception that podcasts are more time-efficient. In the current era of technological technology, utilizing this medium demands less cognitive effort compared to reading and offers a more user-friendly experience. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) refers to a technique used to audibly interpret text that has been retrieved from photographs or PDF files. The proposed methodology involves converting PDF documents into audio files, while eliminating extraneous parts such as headers, footers, page numbers, publisher copyright seals, external references, and other similar components. The approach employs word recognition and textto- speech technology to convert PDF files into audio versions. The process involves employing several technologies such as Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and text-to-speech synthesizers, like Google Text-to-Speech and Python Text-to-Speech, to convert written text into audible audio. The aforementioned technique effectively mitigates the generation of said elements as undesirable outputs within the ultimate audio file. The study at hand aims to assist individuals who are visually impaired and face challenges in reading. Podcast versions of these texts are available for auditory consumption. The proposed methodology aims to achieve the goal of creating a smart environment in which individuals utilize advanced systems to enhance their quality of life.

title: Real-Time Thermal Defect Detection in Additive Manufacturing with Apache Flink
venue: Proceedings of the 19th ACM International Conference on Distributed and Event-Based Systems
abstract: The DEBS 2025 Grand Challenge addresses real-time defect detection in Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) additive manufacturing. Participants must analyze a continuous stream of optical tomography images (per-layer temperature maps) to identify potential defects during the build process. In this paper, we present two stream-processing optimization based on Apache Flink system design that detect defects on-the-fly via local outlier analysis and clustering. The first optimization, termed the offset optimization, precomputes static neighbor offsets to accelerate the calculation of local neighborhood mean temperatures for each pixel. The second optimization, termed the Beta optimization, further improves performance by caching the mean temperatures of “close” neighboring points and updating only those pixels affected when the 3-layer sliding window advances. Implemented in Java on Flink, our approach significantly outperforms the baseline Python implementation provided by the challenge organizers, achieving up to 11{\texttimes

title: Real-Time Threat Detection and Incident Response Using ML
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: With the rise in complex and evolving cyber threats, the need for intelligent, responsive, and resilient intrusion detection systems has become paramount. Traditional security infrastructures often fall short in detecting real-time anomalies and responding swiftly to attacks. To address these critical challenges, we propose a Network-based Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) that integrates machine learning algorithms for real-time monitoring and protection of IT infrastructures. Our system is trained using the NF-UQ-NIDSv2 dataset, enabling the detection and classification of multiple threat vectors such as port scans, SSH brute force attempts, file integrity violations, and Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. Our approach employs a Random Forest model to perform highaccuracy anomaly detection through continuous analysis of system logs and network traffic. Upon identifying a threat, the system autonomously blocks the malicious IP and generates detailed incident alerts for administrators. In addition to threat detection, the system provides robust defense mechanisms, including file integrity monitoring, real-time alert notifications, and user behavior analysis. This ensures not only rapid response but also comprehensive threat management across different layers of the system. Moreover, we implemented the architecture using Python with a modular structure to support scalability and adaptability across varied network environments. Emphasis is placed on automation and minimal manual intervention, ensuring the system can evolve by learning from newly encountered attack patterns. Through this, we aim to significantly enhance the cybersecurity landscape by providing a dynamic, self-learning, and efficient intrusion detection solution capable of defending against modern cyber threats. The inclusion of simulated scenarios for attacks and defenses-such as port scanning, DoS attacks, and file tampering-demonstrates the practical effectiveness and realworld relevance of our propose

title: Real-time Through-water Video Streaming Using a High-rate Underwater Acoustic OFDM System
venue: OCEANS 2023 - Limerick
abstract: Real-time video streaming through the underwater acoustic (UA) channel is challenging due to the limited bandwidth. In this paper, we present a high-rate, reconfigurable software-defined UA communication system that we recently developed, which is capable of real-time through-water video streaming. The transmitter consists of a universal software radio peripheral interfaced with a high-frequency transducer through a broadband impedance matching network designed in house. The transmitter and receiver signal processing algorithms are implemented using Python and run on external host computers. The system can reach a data rate of 445 kbps using a single transducer. The prototype system is tested in a UA communication experiment conducted in a hydroacoustic tank. Experimental results show that together with our video processing algorithms, this system can transmit real-time video with a high quality.

title: Real-time Unstable Approach Detection Using Sparse Variational Gaussian Process
venue: 2020 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics for Air Transportation (AIDA-AT)
abstract: Worldwide, Air Navigation Service Providers (ANSP) are striving to exceed the desired safety levels. The Terminal Manoeuvre Area (TMA) is one of the most safety-critical areas in ATM as it encompasses the most critical phase of flight, i.e., departure and landing. An aircraft, during the final approach phase, is required to remain in a stable configuration and prevent any undesired state such as an unstable approach, which may subsequently lead to incidents/accidents such as Go-Around, Runway Excursions, etc. In this paper, we propose a data-driven framework to model the aircraft 4D trajectories in the final approach phase by adopting sparse variational Gaussian process (SVGP) model. The model is trained to learn the aircraft landing dynamics from Advanced Surface Movement Guidance and Control System (A-SMGCS) data, during the final approach phase. We experimentally demonstrate that SVGP provides an interpretable probabilistic bound of aircraft parameters that can quantify deviation and perform real-time anomaly detection. The findings of this work can increase situational awareness of the air traffic controller and has implications for the design of a new approach procedure in complex runway configurations such as parallel approach.

title: Real-Time Update Cost Monitoring System of BIM Model Supported by Edge Computing
venue: 2025 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Sensors, Electronics and Computer Engineering (ICSECE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of poor real-time performance and low precision of construction project cost monitoring, this paper proposes a real-time update cost monitoring system of BIM model supported by edge computing, and designs a hybrid optimization algorithm based on spatiotemporal weight and reinforcement learning. The system realizes real-time collection and preprocessing of BIM cost data through edge computing nodes to reduce data transmission delay; the hybrid optimization algorithm integrates spatiotemporal weight model and reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust the cost monitoring strategy. In the experiment, a hardware environment consisting of edge servers and Alibaba Cloud ECS instances was built, combined with software platforms such as Revit, Python and TensorFlow, and 1000 sets of actual project BIM data were used as samples for simulation. The results show that compared with the traditional rule-based algorithm, the data update delay of this algorithm is reduced from 5.8 seconds to 2.3 seconds, a reduction of 60.3%; the monitoring error rate is reduced from 15.6% to 8.2%, a reduction of 47.4%; the resource utilization rate of edge nodes reaches 65%, effectively balancing computing performance and resource consumption. Research shows that the system and algorithm significantly improve the real-time and accuracy of construction project cost monitoring, providing a new solution for digital management of the industry.

title: Real-Time Video Analytics at the Edge: Enabling Low-Latency and Scalable Solutions
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Compute, Control, Network & Photonics (ICCCNP)
abstract: This work presents an edge-centric framework for real-time video analytics that is grounded in distributed computing concepts that help to minimize latency and make effective use of bandwidth. The existing, more traditional running of latency-sensitive applications, such as surveillance and traffic management, suffer from high latency and limited scalability; and cloud-based approaches tend to accentuate these issues. To remedy this, our system offloads video processing to the edge and fog nodes using lightweight video processing models, such as YOLOv8 Nano, to allow for quick and local decision-making. Simulations using the iFogSim2 platform have demonstrated improved responsiveness and efficiency in the space and time needed to process the video-based data using various virtual machine (VM) allocation strategies compared to cloud-based implementations. This architecture helps to make efficient use of distributed resources, minimizes network congestion, and improves data privacy. With the contribution of this paper are scalable and responsive edge intelligence solutions that allow for mission-critical, real-time video analytics applications.

title: Real-time video processing using native programming on Android platform
venue: 2012 IEEE 8th International Colloquium on Signal Processing and its Applications
abstract: As the smartphone industry grows rapidly, smartphone applications need to be faster and real-time. For this purpose, most of the smartphone platforms run the program on the native language or compiler that can produce native code for hardware. However for the Android platform that based on the JAVA language, most of the software algorithm is running on JAVA that consumes more time to be compiled. In this paper the performance of native programming and high level programming using JAVA are compared with respect to video processing speed. Eight image processing methods are applied to each frame of the video captured from a smartphone that is running on an Android platform. The efficiencies of the two applications with difference programming language are compared by observing their frame processing rate. The experimental results show that out of the eight images processing methods, six methods that are executed using the native programming are faster than that of the JAVA programming with a total average ratio of 0.41. An application of the native programming for real-time object detection is also presented in this paper. The result shows that with native programming on Android platform, even a complicated object detection algorithm can be done in real-time.

title: Real-Time Video Streaming and Per-Frame Analysis with Qwen2.5-VL for Maritime Surveillance
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Big Data and Algorithms (CAIBDA)
abstract: Real-time video analytics can greatly enhance maritime domain awareness by providing timely insights for applications such as environmental surveillance and vessel monitoring. This paper presents a system for real-time video streaming and per-frame analysis using the Qwen2.5-VL visual-language model (VLM) via API. We describe the system architecture comprising a Python-based video capture and frame queuing pipeline coupled with the Qwen2.5-VL model for image understanding. Both cloud-based and cloud-edge hybrid deployment scenarios are considered: in the cloud, high-performance GPU inference on the VLM achieves low per-frame latency, whereas in edge deployments with limited compute, frames are selectively offloaded to the cloud. We develop theoretical models for key performance indicators including perframe analysis time, end-to-end latency, and frame drop rate, and we validate these with empirical measurements from system logs. In an experimental evaluation, the system processes video frames in near real-time by sampling at approximately 1 frame per second (fps) from a 23fps stream. This achieves manageable latency at the cost of reduced frame fidelity. Results demonstrate the trade-offs between analyzing all frames versus skipping frames for performance, and we discuss strategies to balance timely detection of maritime events (such as boats or pollution) with system constraints.

title: Real-time Virtual Simulation Platform for Multi-UVA hunting target using Deep Reinforcement Learning
venue: 2021 40th Chinese Control Conference (CCC)
abstract: As being one of the most useful flying objects, quadrotor UAVs are gradually being applied to the military field in the form of "swarms". However, an urgent problem is how to improve the intelligence of UAV with low cost. In this paper, we propose a hunting scenario for multi-UAV in an urban environment. Firstly, We build the game model of multi-UAV hunting target and design the reward function. Secondly, we introduce an improved multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) to against an game AI target. Then, we build a virtual platform to simulate the urban combat environment based on the Unity3D game engine. The ML-Agents Toolkit is used to develop a real-time simulation data interface to achieve low-cost model training. Finally, simulation results from Python and virtual environment can demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed hunting scenario.

title: Real-Time Voice Command Recognition System Based on DTW and MFCC
venue: 2023 6th International Conference on Computer Network, Electronic and Automation (ICCNEA)
abstract: Voice command recognition is an important research direction in the field of intelligent speech. Its task is to detect and recognize a given set of command words in continuous speech streams. For command recognition tasks with a voice command vocabulary, this article establishes a real-time voice command recognition system based on DTW and MFCC, using Python tools, to meet the requirements of real-time command recognition tasks. Firstly, the system processes the real-time collected voice based on dynamic time warping (DTW), and then uses the Deep Neural Network (DNN) as a feature extractor to extract the MFCC feature vector of the voice, and calculate the Euclidean distance between the feature vectors of the test voice and the template. The experimental results demonstrate that the real-time speech command recognition system based on DTW and MFCC has comprehensive performance advantages, which can meet the application scenarios of real-time control of speech commands and free users' hands.

title: Real-time web mining application to support decision-making process
venue: 2015 International Conference on Information and Digital Technologies
abstract: This paper describes a solution for the improvement and support of decision-making processes in a reasonable time. It proposes and implements a suitable procedure based on appropriate methods and technologies to create a Web content mining application focused on the trend analysis. The following text describes used architecture, methods and data structures in the context of Web mining and the decision-making approaches. The resulted code runs as a timed script that handles different analyses over the selected Web sites - e.g. the most covered topics in the mass media servers, contexts of the top words based on the distance, saving outputs into the graph, etc. Authors are able to compare options and make decisions very fast, without reading the full contents of the sources. Object-oriented approach is used for the code writing so the code can be easily extended to handle number of different tasks (financial market decisions, crisis management, customer segmentation, social media monitoring, etc.). Real-time analysis of data from different Internet sources and a graphical visualization of results belong to the most important contributions of the proposed application.

title: Real-World Bug Hunting Techniques for Advanced Real-Time IP Address Redirection
venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Mobile Computing and Sustainable Informatics (ICMCSI)
abstract: This research study builds the state-of-art cyber security platform that eventually relied on the internet. It focuses on building this from high-end approaches with practical bug-hunting awareness in its aim toward effective threat detection. It continuously monitors network traffic through several algorithm models for analyzing and stopping malicious activities at real time. In doing this, it blocks and dynamically changes IP addresses in such a way that unwanted access cannot happen. Key Features: Anomaly detection through User and Entity Behavior Analytics, Security Adaptation, Automation, and Response for effective threat management, a threat intelligence feed keeping it abreast of new attack vectors, and the platform comes with deep logging for forensic investigations purposes. Predictive analytics, along with its continuous learning module, allows the detection algorithms to get optimized. Its friendly user interface promotes teamwork, data aggregation, and collective protection and, henceforth, provides the all-encompassing and flexible cybersecurity solution that can help to strengthen the businesses' defenses against constantly changing threats.

title: Realization of nonlinear real-time optimization based controllers on self-contained transfemoral prosthesis
venue: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE Sixth International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Lower-limb prosthesis provide a prime example of cyber-physical systems (CPSs) that interact with humans in a safety critical fashion, and therefore require the synergistic development of sensing, algorithms and controllers. With a view towards better understanding CPSs of this form, this paper presents a methodology for successfully translating nonlinear real-time optimization based controllers from bipedal robots to a novel custom built self-contained powered transfemoral prosthesis: AMPRO. To achieve this goal, we begin by collecting reference human locomotion data via Inertial measurement Units (IMUs). This data forms the basis for an optimization problem that generates virtual constraints, i.e., parametrized trajectories, for the prosthesis that provably yields walking in simulation. Leveraging methods that have proven successful in generating stable robotic locomotion, control Lyapunov function (CLF) based Quadratic Programs (QPs) are utilized to optimally track the resulting desired trajectories. The parameterization of the trajectories is determined through a combination of on-board sensing on the prosthesis together with IMU data, thereby coupling the actions of the user with the controller. Finally, impedance control is integrated into the QP yielding an optimization based control law that displays remarkable tracking and robustness, outperforming traditional PD and impedance control strategies. This is demonstrated experimentally on AMPRO through the implementation of the holistic sensing, algorithm and control framework, with the end result being stable and human-like walking.

title: Recommending unnecessary source code based on static analysis: poster
venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Software Engineering: Companion Proceedings
abstract: Grown software systems often contain code that is not necessary anymore. Unnecessary code wastes resources during development and maintenance, for example, when preparing code for migration or certification. Running a profiler may reveal code that is not used in production, but it is often time-consuming to obtain representative data this way. We investigate to what extent a static analysis approach which is based on code stability and code centrality, is able to identify unnecessary code and whether its recommendations are relevant in practice. To study the feasibility and usefulness of our static approach, we conducted a study involving 14 open-source and closed-source software systems. As there is no perfect oracle for unnecessary code, we compared recommendations of our approach with historical cleanup actions, runtime usage data, and feedback from 25 developers of 5 software projects. Our study shows that recommendations generated from stability and centrality information point to unnecessary code. Our results suggest that static analysis can provide quick feedback on unnecessary code that is useful in practice.

title: Reducing Certification Costs through Assured Dynamic Software Configuration
venue: 2014 IEEE International Symposium on Software Reliability Engineering Workshops
abstract: Engineering activities in the operation and maintenance phase of safety-critical systems are becoming increasingly important. The ever more rising software complexity in terms of an amount of implemented functions led to a proportional increase of various change demands. Most of these demands are initiated to repair the system from defects, i.e., Due to design faults not identified in the development for example. Maintaining changes in the operation phase can be very cost-intensive, because regulations of safety standards recommend to re-verify and re-validate the system in most cases, in order to ensure that the systems integrity is not compromised by the incorporated changes. In this paper, we describe an approach to perform changes on software in the operation and maintenance phase of systems lifecycle. To prevent the impact of changes on systems integrity, certain design limitations are set, so that controlled types of changes are permitted only. Furthermore, since also in cases of strong design limitations the systems integrity can be compromised, a support for systems modelling and analysis has been provided. The modelling captures certain functional and non-functional aspects of the system, which are then analyzed to decide whether changes can be performed or not. The main outcome here is that specific types of changes can be maintained without having an impact on systems integrity and therefore without requiring an extensive re-verification and re-validation. We report on possible improvements in costs of changes, by considering several industrial use cases and their typical change scenarios in the maintenance phase.

title: Reducing the Functional Safety Risks (and Other Risks) That Can Be Caused by EMI — New IEEE Standard 1848
venue: IEEE Letters on Electromagnetic Compatibility Practice and Applications
abstract: When Functional Safety risks must be reduced throughout the lifecycle of an electronic system, the acceptable levels for the risks that could be caused by electromagnetic disturbances or electromagnetic interference (EMI) are about 100dB lower than normal for immunity tests. This means that these risks are incapable of being verified or validated by immunity testing only. At the time of writing, IEEE Standard 1848 is well on its way towards being published. This is a new type of IEEE Standard, and will provide requirements and guidance on the use of well-proven techniques and measures to help ensure that neither electromagnetic disturbances nor EMI will be the cause of unacceptable Functional Safety risks. Its techniques and measures cover: project management; system design; operational design of hardware and software; verification, and validation. They also cover assembly/installation; commissioning, maintenance; upgrade; refurbishment, and disposal. Although intended for reducing Functional Safety risks, the techniques and measures in IEEE 1848 can also be used for reducing any quantifiable risks (mission-critical, reputational, financial, etc.) that could be caused by electromagnetic disturbances or EMI.

title: Reengineering real-time embedded software onto a parallel processing platform
venue: Proceedings of WCRE '96: 4rd Working Conference on Reverse Engineering
abstract: The paper describes a general reengineering process that SED uses as a guideline and the specific reengineering process used in the context of a missile onboard software reengineering experiment. The experiment involves retargeting from a single processor to a scaleable, distributed, multiprocessor implementation. It also discusses the role of a domain specific software architecture, and describes the use of the Honeywell MetaH tool-an automatic code generation tool that was used to automate a significant portion of the software reengineering effort. The conclusions point to areas where reverse engineering technology may be particularly helpful in the context of these process activities.

title: Refactoring Asynchronous Event Handling in the Real-Time Specification for Java
venue: 2009 21st Euromicro Conference on Real-Time Systems
abstract: The primary goal for asynchronous event handling (AEH) in the Real-Time Specification for Java (RTSJ) is to have a lightweight concurrency mechanism. However the RTSJ neither provides a well-defined guideline on how to implement AEH nor requires the documentation of the AEH model used in the implementation. Also the AEH API in the RTSJ are criticized as lacking in configurability as they do not provide any means for programmers to have fine control over the AEH facilities, such as the mapping between real-time threads and handlers. For these reasons, it needs the refactoring of its application programming interface (API) to give programmers more configurability. This paper, therefore, proposes a set of AEH related classes and interfaces to enable flexible configurability over AEH components. We have implemented the refactored configurable AEH API using the new specifications on an existing RTSJ implementation and this paper shows that it allows more configurability for programmers than the current AEH API in the RTSJ does. Consequently programmers are able to specifically tailor the AEH subsystem to fit their applicationspsila particular needs.

title: ReFOCUS+: Multi-Layers Real-Time Intelligent Route Guidance System With Congestion Detection and Avoidance
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Due to random nature of traffic and unpredictability of human behaviors, one of challenging problems in transportation engineering is traffic congestion which has a direct impact on the economy and environment with the increase in traveling time, fuel consumption and emissions. One of approaches to reduce traffic congestions is the advance Route Guidance Systems (RGSs) which can propose alternative optimal routes for vehicles, which are in or will be entering congested roads or areas. Advanced RGSs, usually employ real-time and predicted traffic information of the roads to find the best possible route for vehicles in a way that total traffic congestions will be reduced. In this paper, The ReFOCUS+, a dynamic semi-distributed, multi-layer, and Fog-Cloud based advance route guidance system architecture has been introduced. The ReFOCUS+ architecture, employ Road Side Units (RSUs), to calculate different traffic-related factors such as current and predicted road congestions, area congestions, traveling time, etc. Then, the ReFOCUS+ uses traffic factors to proposes a novel method to detect congested roads in an area and, apply re-routing to vehicles to ease the traffic congestion within each area using a multi-metric fitness function, called Road Weight Measurement (RWM). To evaluate the performance of ReFOCUS+, a new open-source Python-based program has been developed which is able to connect to SUMO traffic simulator and control the simulation. The simulation results demonstrate that ReFOCUS+ outperforms existing solutions and improve traveling time, fuel consumption and gas emissions.11The developed program and software in this paper available at https://www.github.com/hamednoori/ReFOCUS+

title: Reliability and Performance Evaluation of Safety-Critical Instrumentation and Control Systems of Nuclear Power Plant
venue: IEEE Transactions on Reliability
abstract: Instrumentation and control systems are nervous systems of nuclear power plant (NPP). These systems interact with several safety-critical components of the NPP, such as actuators, transformers, control valves, sensors, circuit breakers, signal processing units, controllers, and heat exchangers. Therefore, the failure of these systems could result in significant financial loss, harm to human resources, or environmental damage. As a result, these systems need to be highly reliable and accurate. In this article, we suggest a framework, based on the batch deterministic and stochastic Petri nets (BDSPNs) to measure the reliability and performance of safety-critical system. The framework consists of three phases. In the first phase, the system is modeled using the BDSPN to derive the transition rate among the system states. In phase 2, the transition rate matrix is utilized to compute the steady-state probability values, which help to evaluate the response time of the system using Little's law. The third phase uses a transition probability matrix to assess the reliability of the system. The technique is illustrated on shutdown system of NPP and is validated on the operational profile data. The obtained accuracy of 99.9905% in measurement of reliability validates the approach.

title: Reliability certification of software components
venue: Proceedings. Fifth International Conference on Software Reuse (Cat. No.98TB100203)
abstract: Reuse is pin-pointed as a key factor to improve productivity and reliability of software systems. Verification and validation of software components and the resulting system is important for reuse to be beneficial on a broad industrial basis. The paper suggests a modelling approach which is suitable for reliability certification of modular systems. It discusses a general reliability certification procedure and provides guidelines and opportunities for how to certify software components and also presents some alternatives for certification of modular systems. We conclude that to create reliable systems, we must start certifying the individual constituents of the systems.

title: Reliability Modeling and Verification Method for Dynamic Reconfiguration System
venue: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: A system reliability modeling and verification method based on Finite State Machine (FSM) theory and system failure logic is proposed for Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA) and other dynamic reconfiguration systems. With the reliability modeling of a core processor with dynamic reconfiguration, the method of failure injection experiment is used to test and verify the model. It is confirmed that the method is feasible according to the test results of reliability model and evaluation index.

title: Remote Monitoring of Micro-Hydropower plants using Python
venue: 2024 International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Sustainable Technology (GECOST)
abstract: Hydraulic turbines and synchronous generators are two critical components of micro-hydropower plants, and their maintenance is crucial to ensure the longevity of the system. However, maintenance can be challenging in rural areas where access to facilities is limited, and there is a lack of local expertise to ensure effective ongoing maintenance. To solve this issue, we have developed a permanent remote monitoring system that can monitor various parameters such as rotor speed, rotor mechanical angle, output active power, output reactive power, mechanical power, gate status, current, and voltage phases. The system enables real-time data interpretation and timely intervention for maintenance operations. It is based on an experimental Matlab/Simulink hydroelectric plant model and uses IoT cloud Thingspeak for data storage, LabView for visualization, data analysis, and alert triggering. The system employs HTTP and UDP protocols through a Python program for data transmission. The results obtained from the system are highly satisfactory, making it deployable on real micro-hydropower plants.

title: Requirements-based Code Model Checking
venue: 2020 IEEE Workshop on Formal Requirements (FORMREQ)
abstract: Building the system right is the objective of quality assurance methods. Though testing is the most prominent and widely-adopted means, it cannot prove the absence of software's defects. Therefore, static measures such as formal proofs can complement dynamic methods. However, these techniques require the formal statement of requirements, which is still a challenge in industry development. This paper suggests a way of formalizing requirements in controlled natural language in a way that applies directly to C program code. By mapping natural language terms to conditional breakpoints, requirements can be translated to formal language expressed in observer automata. The creation of a mapping between natural language terms and code is supported by natural language processing methods. Finally, the observer automata are model checked against the code. In our approach we demonstrate the described steps using a set of realistically shaped requirements, which are common in the avionics domain. We implemented a simple tool hiding the abstract and mathematical details, which performs the proofs automatically. The paper is presented as an approach towards the seamless verification of code against requirements typically found in the avionics domain.

title: Research of Prognostic and Health Management for Avionics System Based on Massive Data Mining
venue: 2018 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM-Chongqing)
abstract: The new-generation avionics system is an electronically intensive device. Its complex system structure, multiple failure modes and complex failure mechanism make it difficult to carry out effective fault prediction and health management based on traditional methods. A prognostic and health management (PHM) based on massive data mining of avionics system is presented in this paper. Firstly, the characteristics of the new generation avionics system are analyzed from the aspects of system structure, service environment, and data source and data storage mode. Secondly, the key technologies based on mass data mining are discussed, including data preprocessing, integrated management, diagnosis and prognostic model and so on. Finally, a massive data mining platform of avionics system PHM based on private cloud is proposed. The overall framework, hardware and software structure of the platform are described in detail. The massive data mining platform of avionics system can quickly and effectively carry out data mining, and provide a verification platform for the avionics system PHM, which is of great significance to promote the integration and engineering realization of avionics system PHM.

title: Research on Airworthiness certification of Civil aircraft based on Digital virtual flight test technology
venue: 2019 IEEE/AIAA 38th Digital Avionics Systems Conference (DASC)
abstract: In the process of airworthiness certification for civil aircraft, safety of flight test is the primary precondition for the staff of flight test organization to carry out its work. However, in traditional flight test process, especially in the high-risk flight test subjects, means to ensure flight safety are relatively limited. In addition, the time-consuming flight test cycle and enormous testing points lead to huge time cost and economic cost of civil aircraft in the process of airworthiness certification. In order to solve the above problems, a testing compliance verification method based on digital virtual flight test technology is proposed in this paper. The method has great significance for reducing risk and ensuring safety of flight test. And the number of testing points and costs incurred in flight tests can be greatly depleted if this method is adopted. Moreover, it can also improve the scientific and efficiency of flight test. Digital flight test technology mentioned above refers to carry out human-machine closed-loop simulation of specific assessment flight task by using digital computers. It is based on the mathematical modeling of aircraft dynamics, structure, avionics system and so on, and combined with the pilot model or human-in-the-loop method. According to the simulation results, whether the operation, maneuverability and safety of aircraft flight can meet the airworthiness requirements are investigated. In view of the above idea, digital virtual flight test model and the pilot model should be established to verify the influence of the introduction of digital flight test technology, respectively. Taking stall speed subject as an example, each test point is repeated 6 times in the process of qualified certification of a certain type of aircraft, a total of 228 tests are required. If all test points are completed by means of the conformity test method and 80% of test points are re-tested at the qualification stage (another 20% are in parallel flight

title: Research on Civil Airborne Task Scheduling Test Platform Supporting Provable Data Possession
venue: 2018 Third International Conference on Security of Smart Cities, Industrial Control System and Communications (SSIC)
abstract: Civil airborne test platform for task scheduling generates and stores large amounts of data during the testing phase, but these data may be corrupted due to incorrect operation or malicious behavior. Trying to solve this problem, a civil airborne test platform for task scheduling supporting data integrity verification is proposed in the paper. Firstly the modular architecture of the test platform is presented. Then an algorithm for data integrity verification based on Provable Data Possession (PDP) is described in detail and is integrated into the test platform. Finally, the experimental result shows that the test platform can improve the testing efficiency of the civil airborne software while guaranteeing the integrity of the data.

title: Research on Cross Species Statistical Arbitrage Based on Python
venue: 2022 6th Annual International Conference on Data Science and Business Analytics (ICDSBA)
abstract: Python is widely used in many fields because of its excellent simplicity, readability and scalability. In the field of edible oil, soybean oil and palm oil have great substitutability in the field of consumption, so there is a strong correlation between prices. When the price difference between the two deviates from a certain level, there is an opportunity for cross species arbitrage. Through the correlation analysis and cointegration analysis of the closing prices of futures contracts, the arbitrage position, arbitrage range and stop loss range are determined. Next, using the real data for one and a half years, this paper compiles python code to realize simulated transactions. The simulation results show that the return is 76.5%. It fully demonstrates the power of python and this strategy has good feasibility.

title: Research on Fault Injection Test Technology Based on ARINC429 Avionics Bus
venue: 2025 4th International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: This study proposes a multidimensional fault injection test methodology targeting ARINC429 avionics bus. ARINC429 avionics bus is currently a mature aviation bus standard used in many important onboard systems. Evaluating the reliability and safety of the ARINC429 avionics bus in critical system communication is particularly important. Completing fault injection test and evaluation of ARINC429 signals through injecting specific faults of ARINC429 avionics bus signals into the physical layer, electrical layer, and protocol layer, and completing fault injection test in different scenarios through signal channel routing. This article discusses the principle and architecture of fault injection test for the widely used ARINC429 signal in avionics systems in multi-level and multi scenarios. Based on this architecture, a test platform is built to complete the verification of ARINC429 avionics bus fault injection test. And taking the navigation system as an example, relying on this platform to complete fault injection test.

title: Research on Formal Modeling of Safety Requirements for Airborne Electronic Warfare Software
venue: 2023 CAA Symposium on Fault Detection, Supervision and Safety for Technical Processes (SAFEPROCESS)
abstract: Electronic warfare is the core means to occupy the dominant role of electromagnetic spectrum in war. With the development of advanced components and continuous progress of technology, electronic warfare is facing severe challenges such as complex battle scenes and difficulties in situation signal perception. Once software failure occurs, it will seriously affect the decision of combat mission and the safety of system operation. Formal modeling of software during the requirement phase is an important method to identify and eliminate risks, especially for safety requirements. However, it is difficult to meet the requirements of airborne electronic warfare software by traditional formal modeling method, which cannot guarantee the integrity and adequacy of safety analysis work. In this paper, we improved the traditional formal modeling method by adding considerations on high reliability and strong real-time capability, meeting the requirements of airborne electronic warfare software. Performance of the proposed method was validated by formal modeling the management control system of a certain type of aviation equipment. Compared with traditional formal modeling method, the proposed method was able to find the defects in the software design, such as mutual exclusion of preconditions and loss of abnormal protection, which proved the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method in the field of electronic warfare.

title: Research on GPU Virtualization Scheme in Domestic Embedded Virtualization Platform Based on Rust
venue: 2025 10th International Symposium on Advances in Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering (ISAEECE)
abstract: This paper proposes a lightweight GPU virtualization solution for domestic embedded platforms based on the Rust-based Type-I hypervisor ReVMM. By integrating VFIO passthrough and Mdev-based partitioning, the design achieves efficient GPU sharing with strong isolation and real-time performance. Leveraging Rust’s safety features, the architecture enhances reliability in constrained environments. Preliminary evaluations and security tests validate its effectiveness, offering a promising path for secure and efficient GPU virtualization in embedded scenarios.

title: Research on improved handwriting robot based on Python algorithm
venue: 2024 IEEE 4th International Conference on Information Technology, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (ICIBA)
abstract: Traditional algorithms for writing robots typically rely on pre-defined path planning and precise trajectory control. Due to the reliance on pre-defined paths, the robotic arm may not perform well when dealing with irregular shapes. In contrast, the core of our team's handwriting robot algorithm lies in real-time sampling of trajectories on the screen and converting them into sequences of actions that can be executed by the robotic arm. Firstly, build the hardware part of the handwriting robot, such as the driver and control motherboard, as well as the software part of the robotic arm Python program framework, mainly including communication service module, message processing module, trajectory analysis module, robotic arm inverse solution module, etc. On this basis, geometric analysis of the robotic arm mechanism is carried out, and the program operation is determined by observing the angles of each joint, followed by trajectory planning. This method not only improves real-time performance and accuracy, but also enables the writing robot to adapt to display devices of different resolutions and screen sizes. In daily life, it can be applied to automatic writing and drawing, such as automatic signature or drawing of fine art works.

title: Research on Knowledge Extraction and Modeling of Engineering Model Contracts Based on Collective Intelligence Collaboration
venue: 2025 8th International Conference on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (BDAI)
abstract: Engineering contract management faces the double bottleneck of low efficiency of manual audit and lack of flexibility of automation technology: manual audit is inefficient and poorly reproducible due to the large volume of text and complex semantic correlation of clauses, and automation technology is limited by engineering terminology barriers and long-range semantic dependence. In order to break through this dilemma, this study innovatively introduces the paradigm of group intelligence collaboration, and puts forward the fusion intelligence path of “human designing the knowledge framework → machine executing the data processing →human verifying and optimizing”: firstly, integrating the wisdom of expert groups, systematically analyzing the text of the demonstration contract, refining 15 types of scenarios and 200 events, and constructing a system of 350+ universal keywords; then developing a system based on the keyword system. Then, it develops Python-based intelligent extraction pipeline to realize automated positioning and structured encapsulation of contract terms through title-text semantic unit parsing and keyword matching matrix; finally, after verification and optimization by the expert group, it builds a structured knowledge base covering 208 attribute fields and 350+ terms in MySQL. Empirical evidence shows that the method breaks through the traditional path limitations and provides a scalable intelligent solution for engineering contract risk control.

title: Research on Multi-layer Resource Allocation and Real-time Scheduling Model of Digital Economy Platform for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 2nd International Conference on Digital Economy and Computer Science
abstract: The “one size fits all” resource allocation strategy of existing digital economy platforms further exacerbates the contradiction between “resource idle” and “demand thirst” for SMEs (small and medium-sized enterprises). Given the crucial role of resource allocation and scheduling in the efficient operation of digital economy platforms, this paper conducts research on a multi-layer resource allocation and real-time scheduling model for SMEs in digital economy platforms. Firstly, aiming at the fragmentation, high volatility and cross-layer collaborative demand of SMEs, a multi-layer resource allocation model based on digital twinning and dynamic value evaluation is constructed. The model includes physical resource layer, virtualized resource layer and service orchestration layer. The dynamic mapping relationship between physical resources and service requirements is established through the resource value function, and the cross-layer resource constraints are defined, with the optimization goal of maximizing the total value. Secondly, a hybrid real-time scheduling model (DRL-GNN) based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and graph neural network (GNN) is designed to meet the requirements of millisecond response and high fluctuation. Model the resource allocation problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), utilize Graph Neural Networks (GNN) to construct a resource graph and capture topological dependencies among resources to enhance the state representation in Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), adopt the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm as the DRL method, and explicitly define the real-time scheduling process. Finally, a simulation platform is built based on Python 3.9, PyTorch framework and Gymnasium, and a desensitized workload data set of a public cloud platform is used to compare with three baseline schemes: static reservation strategy, GA-Heuristic scheduling based on genetic algorithm and DRL-Only scheduling without GNN. The results show that DRL-GNN

title: Research on Safety Analysis Method of Functional Integrated Avionics Systems
venue: 2018 IEEE/AIAA 37th Digital Avionics Systems Conference (DASC)
abstract: Confronted with difficulties in the safety status analysis of avionics systems attributed to functional integration, a new safety analysis method based on a denoising-improved deep belief network, a deep learning algorithm, is proposed, realizing the mapping of system status parameters to overall system safety status within the context of multiple dimensions. By setting the aircraft environment surveillance system (AESS) as an instance, the engineering data was utilized to verify the feasibility of the method, yielding high classification performance. Comparative experiments with original DBN, DSAE, and NN demonstrated that the proposed method can achieve safety status identification directly from complex original data, and possesses strong classification robustness.

title: Research on Satellite Communication System Design and Verification of Civil Aircraft
venue: 2024 10th Asia Conference on Mechanical Engineering and Aerospace Engineering (MEAE)
abstract: With the development of satellite communication (SATCOM) in aviation industry, satellite communication is used more and more widely in civil aircrafts. SATCOM is composed of different airborne equipment and has complex interconnections with other airborne systems, like Inertial Reference System (IRS), Global Position System (GPS), Radio Tuning System, Audio Integrating System, etc. It is a challenge for aircraft integrators to ensure each part of SATCOM system can be designed appropriate to fulfill its intended function according to limitations specified (like Antennas) without any interference with the other airborne systems. Meanwhile, the airworthiness process should also be taken into account after the satellite communication system has been installed, to show the design features can meet the expected provisions. This paper analyzes the airworthiness provisions and provides compliance approaches and activities of satellite communication system after being installed, from the system description, architectural analysis and the aural and visual alerts design, which provides guidance for the design and verification of satellite communication systems of civil aircrafts.

title: Research on the application of openstack to build a new heterogeneous real-time virtual cloud to reproduce application vulnerability and training demonstration architecture
venue: 2017 IEEE 2nd Information Technology, Networking, Electronic and Automation Control Conference (ITNEC)
abstract: In order to cope with the issues that physical hardware conditions and virtualized technical restrictions, Information Security Laboratory, Electric Power Research Institute, the State Gird Xinjiang Electric Power Company, where adopts virtualization and cloud technologies as well as uses the python and openstack to build out a fire-new, heterogeneous and real-time virtual cloud (NHRVC), reproducing the vulnerability attack and its processes in application systems for showing a network security technology platform. The platform adopts three equipments to establish: the physical network device, the safety device and the virtual cloud equipment. These based on layered abstract design and regional management. This platform has the characteristics, such as clear construction that it is easy to set up simulation and migrate complicated application systems. After the second-deployment, the application systems can make many snapshots from different stages and different physical application environments to pursue penetration testing in the total azimuth and the total process through the cloud experiment platform. At the same time, it can friendly carry on display and analysis to the process of the penetration testing.

title: Research on the Construction and Optimization of Comprehensive Quality Evaluation Model for Private College Teachers Based on AHP and Python
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Future Education
abstract: In the new era, different requirements have been imposed on the comprehensive quality of teachers in private colleges. This paper applies Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to establish an evaluation model for the comprehensive quality of teachers in private colleges in the new era. It implements matrix operations and weight calculation based on Python programming, optimizing the implementation efficiency of the traditional AHP algorithm. A dynamic weight update mechanism is designed, which adjusts the index weights in real time by integrating educational big data, thereby realizing the automation of data input, consistency check, and weight update. This paper provides an evaluation model that meets the requirements of the new era and an efficient implementation solution for analyzing the key indexes in the evaluation of teachers' comprehensive quality in private colleges. This enables colleges to better improve teachers' comprehensive quality and cultivate talents suitable for the development of the times.

title: Research on the Evaluation Model of Automatic Real-Time Data Processing for Interpreting Quality Based on Artificial Intelligence
venue: 2025 5th Asia-Pacific Conference on Communications Technology and Computer Science (ACCTCS)
abstract: This paper proposes an automatic real-time data processing evaluation model for interpreting quality based on artificial intelligence, aiming to achieve efficient quality monitoring through natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning technology. The system combines data processing and language correction algorithms to analyze the quality of interpreted texts in real time in multiple dimensions. Specifically, the model design includes modules such as semantic matching, syntactic structure analysis, and sentiment attitude determination, and optimizes the performance of the model in different contexts through data-driven optimization. To verify the effectiveness of the model, this paper conducted many simulation tests and evaluated the model using precise data analysis methods. In the test data set, the model performed better than traditional methods in terms of real-time and accuracy of interpreting, with an accuracy improvement of 12% and a feedback speed improvement of about 35%. The experimental results show that the model has significant advantages in stability, accuracy and adaptability, and can significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of interpreters and meet the needs of practical applications.

title: Research on the Real-time Calculation Method of safety factor of Tailings Dam Based on Monitoring Data
venue: 2022 8th International Conference on Hydraulic and Civil Engineering: Deep Space Intelligent Development and Utilization Forum (ICHCE)
abstract: Stability analysis is an important method to estimate the safety of tailings dam, In order to monitor the real-time safety of the tailings dam, this study establishes the dynamic modeling technology of the tailings dam outer profile model based on the monitoring data such as the beach crest elevation, the outer dam slope ratio, and others data of the tailings dam online monitoring system, uses the preliminary optimization algorithm of profile to generate the generalized zones of the cross section of tailings dam, and then employs the discrete point results of phreatic line monitoring data to fit the phreatic line curve of tailings dam based on the theoretical calculation formula of spatial distribution curve of phreatic line, finally uses Python language to develop the real-time calculation module of tailings dam safety factor, thus realizing the real-time calculation of tailings dam safety factor based on the outer profile monitoring data and phreatic line real-time monitoring data.

title: Resilience by design is mandatory to support the certification of the embedded/artificial intelligence of an autonomous swarm of drones
venue: 2020 AIAA/IEEE 39th Digital Avionics Systems Conference (DASC)
abstract: Several armies and private companies are considering swarms of drones [1], [2] as a mean to achieve missions on theatres of operations [3] because they offer several advantages. For instance, they make it possible to support continuous flight and they offer features that a single system cannot provide [4]. To be fully effective, a swarm should be autonomous, i.e. it should be able to take its own decisions in response to external or internal events, which requires some sort of embedded intelligence. Embedded intelligence is not artificial intelligence (AI) in itself, but it gives birth to a form of AI when autonomy is at play. A major characteristic (some would say drawback, but it is the prize to pay for the above advantages) of this kind of swarm, when considering a large number of aircraft, is that failure is the nominal mode of operation [5], because the more aircraft, the higher the probability of failure. The problem is that failure is by definition an obstacle towards certification, which is a sinequanon condition to the wide deployment of these complex systems. It is therefore crucial to consider failure from the start of application design. We show below that distribution and resilience are key topics to address.

title: Resolution Scaled Quality Adaptation for Ensuring Video Availability in Real-time Systems
venue: 2012 IEEE 14th International Conference on High Performance Computing and Communication & 2012 IEEE 9th International Conference on Embedded Software and Systems
abstract: Online videos are one of the most prevalent forms of communication over the Internet because humans are attracted to visual stimulations. Multimedia services, especially real-time services, require data to arrive on time. Unlike any other transmissions, video streaming needs to be monitored and adapted to bandwidth, when the video stream passes through the best-effort environment. A guaranteed QoS (Quality of Service) is essential in all real-time applications. This paper presents a contextaware mechanism, which improves the QoS of real time video transmission, over wireless networks. This proposed RSQA system ensures video availability even when the bandwidth is low. Drawbacks to other solutions for saving bandwidth in real-time include being: 1) too expensive due to requiring a priority based router (in the case of proxy based and frame prioritization approaches); 2) too complex; 3) not appropriate for real-time systems. This RSQA system succeeds in being of low complexity, appropriate for real-time systems and cost effective (not requiring a priority based router to function). This RSQA system is independent of wireless technology making, thus it appropriate for use in a heterogeneous environment as well. Whenever a user experiences packet loss or a delay in receiving a video, the server will be notified about the congestion and decrease the video quality to make the video available at low bandwidth. The decision regarding the needed QoS parameters and the rate control is based on context information (available bandwidth). The RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) based streaming is simulated and verified by an Eclipse simulator and Java using an MJPEG standard. Results show that the QoS parameters of video transmission were improved considerably by this RSQA system.

title: Resource management for enhancing predictability in systems with limited processing capabilities
venue: 2010 IEEE 15th Conference on Emerging Technologies & Factory Automation (ETFA 2010)
abstract: There is an increasing demand for computing systems composed by heterogeneous computers, connected by different types of networks, and that allow for accessing a wide range of services in a seamless way. Some of those computers are mobile or embedded and have limited resources, and can be overloaded when trying to handle their users demands. Then it is not possible to ensure a proper behaviour of the running applications. This can be an important problem when dealing with critical events in healthcare, home surveillance, or forest monitoring. Resource reservation is a valid basis for handling this issue. It allows for guaranteeing a certain resource share for applications that are important for the proper behavior of a given system. This paper describes an implementation of a resource management component and its integration in the Linux kernel. This piece of software has allowed to assign CPU budgets to standard Java threads, which is an important facility, given the widespread of this programming language. This implementation has been validated on service oriented middleware, where relevant services are executed by thread with guaranteed budget, to improve its predictability.

title: Restricting IEC 61131-3 programming languages for use on high integrity applications
venue: 2008 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation
abstract: When developing applications with high integrity requirements, the choice of programming language is of utmost importance. In fact, IEC 61508 includes a table with suggested programming languages for each SIL (safety integrity level). The languages defined in IEC 61131-3 are included in this table, but are only highly recommended for the higher SILs if a subset of the languages are used. In this paper we propose restrictions and changes to the IEC 61131-3 languages that constitute a subset of the languages with the objective of making them appropriate for the development of high integrity applications.

title: Revealing the Unseen: AI Chain on LLMs for Predicting Implicit Dataflows to Generate Dataflow Graphs in Dynamically Typed Code
venue: ACM Trans. Softw. Eng. Methodol.
abstract: Dataflow graphs (DFGs) capture definitions (defs) and uses across program blocks, which is a fundamental program representation for program analysis, testing and maintenance. However, dynamically typed programming languages like Python present implicit dataflow issues that make it challenging to determine def-use flow information at compile time. Static analysis methods like Soot and WALA are inadequate for handling these issues, and manually enumerating comprehensive heuristic rules is impractical. Large pre-trained language models (LLMs) offer a potential solution, as they have powerful language understanding and pattern matching abilities, allowing them to predict implicit dataflow by analyzing code context and relationships between variables, functions, and statements in code. We propose leveraging LLMs’ in-context learning ability to learn implicit rules and patterns from code representation and contextual information to solve implicit dataflow problems. To further enhance the accuracy of LLMs, we design a five-step chain of thought (CoT) and break it down into an Artificial Intelligence (AI) chain, with each step corresponding to a separate AI unit to generate accurate DFGs for Python code. Our approach’s performance is thoroughly assessed, demonstrating the effectiveness of each AI unit in the AI Chain. Compared to static analysis, our method achieves 82% higher def coverage and 58% higher use coverage in DFG generation on implicit dataflow. We also prove the indispensability of each unit in the AI Chain. Overall, our approach offers a promising direction for building software engineering tools by utilizing foundation models, eliminating significant engineering and maintenance effort, but focusing on identifying problems for AI to solve.

title: Review Analysis Real Time Implementation of Hand Gesture Recognition Model
venue: 2023 International Conference on Computer Science and Emerging Technologies (CSET)
abstract: Hand gesture recognition is a pivotal area of research with numerous applications in human-computer interaction, augmented reality, and robotics. This research paper presents a real-time implementation of a hand gesture recognition model designed to accurately and efficiently interpret hand gestures in real-world scenarios. Due to its adaptability and user-friendliness, hand gesture recognition is one of the most recent and happening study area in terms of human-computer interface. The development of a system that can be used to communicate with disabled individuals or to operate a device using the gesture recognition approach. High intergroup similarities in hand gesture poses, light variance, non-uniform backgrounds, and user-specific hand size and shape variations present significant hurdles for the development of an effective hand gesture identification algorithm. The given research paper represents a basic technique that could be used to develop a hand gesture recognition technique along with cursor movements. On three benchmark static hand gesture datasets with uniform and irregular backdrops for the CV2 tests, a thorough analysis is conducted.
